#1487. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. #1486. First Anfield victory for 14 years was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Fleetwood humbling. His Arsenal look the finished article - Liverpool were authors of their own downfall, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 13:54 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:32 EDT, 2 November 2026

Five nights ago, 40 miles to the north of Anfield at a remote outpost of English football, Arsenal fell to one of the most humiliating reverses of their long and august history. In the teeth of a gale that blew in off the Irish Sea, they were knocked out of the League Cup by Fleetwood Town, a team 18th in League Two.

They left with their tails between their legs, their teenage prodigy Max Dowman sent off in a melee, their heart questioned, their quality debated, their discipline an issue. Mikel Arteta and his side knew that just a few days later, at the other end of the Fylde Coast and across the Ribble Estuary, they would have to swap running the gauntlet of the Cod Army for the challenge of facing down the roar of the Kop.

They did not shirk it. If Tuesday night was a humbling, their gritty 1-0 victory in an Anfield that was a cauldron once more felt like a significant triumph. It was a defensive masterclass from the champions, an exercise in indomitability. It was their first victory here since 2012 and it took them above Manchester City so that they sit, once more, at the top of the table. Liverpool could not summon a single shot on target.

‘It felt like the end of the world when we were knocked out at Fleetwood,’ Arteta said after this win. ‘You look so silly. I was thinking “How can I lift these players up?” You have to dig deep. This was a mission to win here and it is something that we have not done for 14 years for a variety of reasons. We knew we would have to navigate some difficult moments.’

If Arteta left Fleetwood answering questions about his management of Dowman, he finished this game by striding on to the pitch after the final whistle, pumping his fists in front of the Arsenal fans celebrating in the Anfield Road end, and beating his hand on his chest. This was a vindication for him and his team. Five nights is a long time in football.

He had talked about the harsh realities of this sport after Tuesday’s loss. He had reminded everyone that playing at this level was not like ‘Disneyland’. And this victory was not like Disneyland, either. It was less a theme park and more an assault course. It was rough and it was unforgiving and Arsenal were equal to it.

Liverpool, improving under the management of Andoni Iraola, had been talked up as title contenders ahead of this match on a dank evening on Merseyside where the streets around the ground were decorated with the toothless grimaces of rotting pumpkins on doorsteps. The home team showed exhilarating signs of their re-emergence as an attacking force.

They dominated much of the game, too, but they looked like an emerging team, a team that is still evolving. Arsenal, marshalled imperiously by Declan Rice, looked like the finished article. They created one outstanding chance and Kai Havertz converted it. That was all they needed.

Their defence stayed rock-solid, although there was some puzzlement that Liverpool were not awarded a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt-pull on Alexander Isak. After the interval, Liverpool rarely looked like drawing level.

Kai Havertz gave the Gunners a lead to defend after finishing off a well worked move early on

The German slotted home after Declan Rice fizzed a dangerous ball across the six-yard box

Winning at Anfield was vindication for Mikel Arteta after Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood Town

The opening had been predictably frenetic. Neither team forged a chance but Trey Nyoni, who has forced his way into the first team with a series of excellent performances in midfield, could have been booked twice inside the first quarter of an hour.

The initial infringement was a nasty tackle on Martin Odegaard inside the first minute where he planted his studs in Odegaard’s ankle. The second was a spiteful tackle on Kai Havertz. Neither received a yellow card, which gave yet more pause for thought about the red card shown to Dowman at Fleetwood, and its aftermath.

Let’s get one thing straight – the criticism of Arteta for his ‘treatment’ of Dowman was absurd. It has come to something when a manager giving a player a hard stare is interpreted by some as a disproportionate response.

Nobody is necessarily hankering after a return to the days of Sir Alex Ferguson’s hairdrier or Joe Kinnear’s rants that broke records for expletives but if a boss is attracting censure because he looked at a player a bit funny, we are in big trouble.

Arteta is not there to indulge Dowman. He is there to coach him and to teach him and to help him grow up in the context of a Premier League football club. His actions in Fleetwood on Tuesday fulfilled his obligations in all of those criteria.

Arsenal survived the initial frenzy here and took the lead after 16 minutes. Liverpool were the authors of their own downfall. They gave the ball away from a goal kick, it was worked to Noni Madueke on the right, and when Madueke fed it to Declan Rice on the overlap, Rice crossed beautifully for Havertz, who touched it home at the back post.

Arsenal nearly returned the favour a minute later when they played themselves into trouble at the back. Bradley Barcola found himself through on David Raya but his first touch let him down and Rice moved across to clear the danger.

Alexis Mac Allister was left with his head in his hands after missing a glorious chance to score

Liverpool's 19-year-old talent Trey Nyoni started the match but was replaced in the second half

Liverpool recovered and began to dominate the game. Barcola’s pace began to cause Arsenal all sorts of problems down their right flank and Liverpool came close to an equaliser when Virgil van Dijk flicked on a corner and Alexander Isak was denied by the brave intervention of Raya.

Arsenal were still threatening on the counter. Christos Tzolis chipped a ball to the back post and, as Liverpool scrambled to clear it, Madueke turned it back across goal. The ball was intended for Havertz, who was unmarked in the middle, but Timber could not get out of the way of it and it bounced off him into touch.

The atmosphere was febrile. Liverpool had three appeals for penalties, first for Timber’s shirt pull on Isak, then for challenges on Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo, turned down in quick succession. Tempers began to flare on the benches.

The breathlessness of the match was relentless. Florian Wirtz drove a free kick against the face of the crossbar with Raya beaten and then, three minutes before the interval, Mac Allister ran on to a cross from Milos Kerkez and, with the goal at his mercy, directed his free header too high.

Liverpool laid siege to the Arsenal goal after the break but the openings just would not come. Isak blazed high over the bar from an angle, Wirtz had a shot on the turn blocked and then, just before the hour, Dominik Szoboszlai replaced Nyoni and, to more acclaim, Rio Ngumoha came on for Gakpo.

Still Liverpool could not prise Arsenal open. Arsenal began to grow in confidence and threat. The home team were grateful to Jeremy Jacquet for a clearance that prevented Odegaard turning Tzolis’s cross into an open goal, for Van Dijk’s brilliant interception to deny Havertz and, most of all, for a quite magnificent one-handed save from Alisson that diverted a Tzolis shot round the post. It will stand the test of time as one of the saves of the season.

Arsenal put in another excellent defensive display to frustrate and keep Liverpool at bay

Liverpool’s frustration boiled over. Mac Allister was booked for his part in an ugly fracas with Odegaard and Madueke. The stands became a mass of pointing fingers and shouts of protest and anger. Time-wasting and play-acting peppered the match. Liverpool felt the game slipping away in the angst.

Liverpool threw everything at it in the final minutes. Lewis Koumas flung himself at a bouncing ball but could not get enough power on his header, Ngumoha had a shot charged down, Barcola desperately searched for pockets of space but could not find them. There were six minutes of time added on but there was no way through. Arsenal’s defence would not yield.

#1485. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

Francesco Camarda shared some words to try inspire the stars of the future during an event on Tuesday afternoon.

Camarda was present at the Paolo and Larissa Pini Institute for a one-on-one discussion with students and a lesson with the Sport and Health tutors, to help promote the value of sport and the desire to continue practicing it.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was the player who asked the students questions for the most part, not the other way around. Camarda questioned them on their motivations behind playing sports, if they have ever considered quitting and if so why they chose to continue.

After the discussion, the practical part of the program began, with a physical activity lesson led by Sport e Salute tutors, in collaboration with Adidas too. Camarda spoke to some reporters present at the event, with his words via MilanNews.

“When you play football, you learn that you don’t have to do everything alone: ​​you have team-mates, someone to help you, and someone who relies on you. And it’s not important to be the best to feel part of the team,” he said.

A post shared by MilanNews.it (@milannewsitofficial)

“That’s the beauty of sport: it gives you the chance to test yourself, have fun, and improve, even when you don’t succeed at something.

“If I can leave a message to the kids, it’s to not be afraid to try and not to think that sport is only for those who want to become a professional. It’s an experience that can give so much to everyone.”

Camarda himself is having to be patient and to wait for opportunities at the moment given his lack of playing time under Ruben Amorim, which may even mean evaluating another loan move away from his boyhood club.

#1483. Premier League: Tottenham tames Chelsea and finally launches its season

Tottenham finally has its benchmark match. After a particularly complicated start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi’s Spurs traveled to Stamford Bridge this Saturday with the ambition of confirming their first success of the season in the Premier League, obtained on the previous day against Coventry (3-1). But the task looked particularly delicate against Chelsea, fourth before the match and winner of the last six London derbies between the two teams in the league. Deprived of João Pedro, Xabi Alonso’s Blues lined up Rogers up front with Quenda, Neto and Palmer behind him while De Zerbi decided to start Mathys Tel on the left side of his attack. A profitable choice in the offensive animation of the visitors, who quickly displayed a much more attractive face than during their previous outings.

Because contrary to expectations, Tottenham took control of the game from the first minutes. The Spurs increased the sequences of possession and collective movements, with a particularly inspired James Maddison between the lines. Mohammed Kudus first tried his luck without finding the target, before Chelsea responded with Cole Palmer, whose shot was brilliantly saved by Antonín Kinský (15th). But the biggest chance of the first act went to Omar Marmoush. Perfectly served behind by Andrew Robertson after a combination with Mathys Tel, the Egyptian striker missed his face-to-face by shooting directly at Mike Penders (30th). Very restless, Tel also caused problems for Acheampong on his side, actively participating in the domination of Spurs. Despite several interesting situations, the two teams returned to the locker room with a goalless draw.

Returning from the locker room, Tottenham continued to show good intentions, despite the injury exit of James Maddison, replaced by Conor Gallagher. Chelsea tried to regain control of the proceedings, but the visitors maintained a real collective solidity while continuing to project themselves forward. And the efforts of Roberto De Zerbi’s men were finally rewarded in the 77th minute. On a corner hit by Mateus Fernandes, Mike Penders completely missed his aerial intervention under pressure from Jan Paul van Hecke, sending the ball into his net himself (0-1). A huge blow for the Blues, whose evening changed again three minutes later with the expulsion of Cole Palmer. Already warned in the first period, the England international received a second yellow card after a sole on Conor Gallagher (80th), leaving his partners at ten for the final minutes.

In numerical superiority, Tottenham then sought to make the break. Gallagher notably created a good opportunity, repelled by Penders, before Sandro Tonali sent his recovery over the top (85th). Mathys Tel also continued to provoke on his wing before being rewarded. On a solitary rush, he came to offer the second goal to his team. Solid until the end, Spurs preserved their advantage to win at Stamford Bridge (0-2) and end a series of six consecutive defeats against their London rival in the championship. A major success which allows Tottenham, sixteenth before this eighth day, to leave the red zone and distance themselves from the last places. Conversely, Chelsea are letting precious points slip away in the race for first places. Above all, Roberto De Zerbi finally saw his team combine collective mastery, quality of play and defensive efficiency. Enough to look forward to the rest of the season with greater optimism.

#1480. Gabriel and Mac Allister's cheating is not just embarrassing, it's malevolent and wicked... players need the threat of red cards for such dishonesty and - if that fails - punishments after review, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 18:05 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:37 EDT, 2 November 2026

Football’s lawmakers like to meddle. The problem is they do it in areas that tend not to need any meddling. Like around handball and offside and other places that were doing just fine as they were.

So here’s a tip for the meddlers at the International Football Association Board. Meddle somewhere that needs it. Meddle in a way that would be meaningful and important and in a way that would actually help the game.

Please meddle with cheating. Please do something that would spare us from the embarrassment of grown men behaving like children in a bid to get other players booked and sent off. Yes, please meddle there.

Because football at the top level really needs it.

It needs a route through which players such as Alexis Mac Allister and Gabriel Magalhaes can be properly punished, shamed and embarrassed for what they did during Sunday’s otherwise fabulous Premier League game between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield.

It needs a deterrent. It needs greater power to match referees and greater leeway for retrospective punishment.

Alexis Mac Allister drops to the floor holding his face after his forehead is slightly brushed

The Liverpool man tried to get Noni Madueke sent off during Arsenal's 1-0 victory at Anfield

In a way, it is handy that there was one from each team this time. That way, we can be spared the usual accusations of bias that tend to come when footballers are called out for their sins.

Here, live on TV, Gabriel and Mac Allister were both as bad as each other. One in each half, clear as day.

Arsenal defender Gabriel was poked in the chest early on by Aleksandar Isak and went down holding his face. Then, much later, Liverpool’s Mac Allister was brushed by the forehead of Noni Madueke and did likewise.

Neither fooled referee Andy Madley. Both were told to get up and get on with the game. On TV, Sky Sports analysts Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher didn’t hold back.

‘Embarrassing’ was the word they both chose. Neville to describe Gabriel and Carragher as a way of calling out Mac Allister.

But this type of chicanery is more than that. We see it from lots of players and we see it all the time. It’s not just embarrassing. It goes much deeper. It’s malevolent. It’s low. It’s pre-meditated. It’s wicked.

Short of dark subjects such as spitting and leg-breaking tackles, I can’t think of much worse things on a football field than pretending to have a head or facial injury when you actually haven’t.

So where IFAB need to get involved – where they need to ‘meddle’ – is simple. They must increase football’s powers to punish.

On the field and in the moment, referees can issue yellow cards for simulation and for cheating. Players can be booked for exaggerating contact (Mac Allister) or pretending contact has been made with a certain area of the body when it hasn’t (Gabriel).

Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes performed a similar act of cheating in the first half

The Brazilian fell down clutching his face after Alexander Isak brushed his neck and chest

But why is there no power – at least in occasional and exceptional circumstances - to issue a red card?

Gabriel and Mac Allister appeared to be trying to get their opponents sent off. Would they do it if they knew the match referee at least had the option of showing them the red card instead?

Retrospectively, meanwhile, we need greater leeway for action.

Under a law passed a decade ago, a player can theoretically be banned by a review panel for two-games for ‘successful deception of a match official’. However the reality is that the initiative has largely been superseded by VAR and was only really used for players diving to try and win penalties anyway.

In terms of the nonsense we witnessed at Anfield on Sunday – and indeed see on a reasonably regular basis around the country – there is very little recourse once the game is over so once again a possible deterrent has been removed from the equation.

Cheating of this nature currently looks and feels like a risk worth taking and that is what must change.

Alexander Isak was not given a penalty despite being blatantly pulled back by Jurrien Timber

Here, it was interesting to hear Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola suggest afterwards that he must start telling his players to go down under contact. He was talking about Isak’s refusal to buckle under a clear penalty area shirt tug from Jurrien Timber.

That’s an important issue, too. Players should not be punished for their honesty. A foul is a foul, regardless of the reaction. VAR should have awarded a penalty.

But here on an otherwise fine day for the Premier League, another known and rather ugly blot on the landscape grew larger.

The threat of red cards for cheating and – if that fails - punishments handed down by review. That’s the kind of meddling we should all be on board with.

Despite the injuries that slowed down his career, the Parisian never stopped working to regain his best level. A determination that commands the respect of his former teammate.

“His return to the top? I’m not surprised. I know the efforts he makes every day to be ready when we call on him. In training, for example, he is always at full speed. He’s a huge competitor, confirms Pavard. You get the impression that he’s always there laughing, but when you have to get hurt, he’s always there. He gives his all, whether as a starter or if he only plays five minutes. He’s a guy who is always at the service of the collective and someone who is reliable”explained the player who passed through OM.

#1478. Ballon d’Or 2026: France Football tackles PSG

Another year, a funny evening for Paris Saint-Germain, who played their Ligue 1 match against Olympique Lyonnais right in the middle of this Ballon d’Or ceremony. A solid 2-0 victory for the Parisians, which logically pleased the Ile-de-France supporters. But it must be said that what happened in London also irritated more than one person on social networks…

Indeed, if the reigning European champion was logically elected best club of the year 2026, the Parisian players finished quite far from the leading roles in the final ranking of this 2026 Ballon d’Or. The first Parisian, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, is sixth, while Ousmane Dembélé follows him, in seventh position. Fabian Ruiz is tenth, while Achraf Hakimi and Vitinha finished thirteenth and fourteenth respectively. Next come Willian Pacho (20th), Nuno Mendes (23rd) and Marquinhos (25th). For many fans, the Parisian players were not respected and finished too low in the rankings.

Asked by The Evening Teamthe editor-in-chief of France Football Vincent Garcia mentioned the Parisian case. “Mbappé had a very good campaign in real life. He was able to explain well and put people and jurors in the heads, because it didn’t come down to much. He knew how to capitalize on what he had done in a World Cup year. The proof, it didn’t amount to much”he explained. What does this have to do with Paris Saint-Germain? Well according to him, unlike its former star, PSG mismanaged its communication.

“Others had a less good campaign. I think a little about PSG. They are double European champions, we have Kvara sixth, Ousmane seventh, Fabian Ruiz tenth. I find that PSG’s communication was perhaps not very clear in trying to promote three players, then two. For me, I would point out that it’s not my job, I don’t do communications, but they should have worked for a player. They should have ridden for the title holder, Ousmane Dembélé”confided the journalist. The message got through.

#1477. Top Gun, tears, thrills and the future script: Cardinale the leading actor in rollercoaster visit

When he touched down in Italy before the Udinese game, not even Gerry Cardinale himself will have foreseen the whirlwind week that followed.

The visit of the Milan owner was known about ahead of time, as were his motivations. Cardinale not only wanted to demonstrate his closeness to the team in a very important moment, but he also had a lot of off-field issues to tackle too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He would end up staying in the country for one week, something that has not been common. This is a different version of the RedBird Capital founder that we are seeing though, one that seems more hands-on than ever when it comes to steering the ship.

Or rather, in this case, it was a bit of a rollercoaster that he was at the front of. It started with a climb, continued with a steep drop, and then came the ascent which ultimately led into take-off on his flight back to America.

Things started quite well for Cardinale in his latest visit, as Milan went away to Udinese and won 2-0 thanks to goals from Christian Pulisic and Omari Hutchinson, bouncing back well from the defeat in Bournemouth a few nights prior.

Attention then shifted to the midweek meeting with a resurgent Bologna side at San Siro, and things did not go as well. Alphadjo Cisse’s brace was ultimately outshone by Samuel Mbangula’s hat-trick, as the Rossoblu scored three unanswered second-half goals to win 4-2.

It was a crash back down to earth, and a further reminder that this team remains very much a work in progress, with obvious limitations and shortcomings that can be exploited in quite a ruthless way. With the loss, Milan moved seven points off the leaders Inter and Lazio.

A few days ago, after the win in Udine, Cardinale had praised both the team and Ruben Amorim in a post-match interview. After the Bologna game, the owner not only didn’t speak, but left the stadium looking rather glum to say the least.

Sometimes, though, the curses can be a blessing too. Perhaps this was a necessary reminder for everyone – from Cardinale down to the players – that there is no shortcut with this project, and that there will be growing pains.

It cannot be argued though that it set a rather gloomy backdrop to everything that would come in the next few days, which makes what actually happened all the more remarkable.

The big day finally arrived on Thursday, just 24 hours after the Bologna match: Milan and Inter unveiled the renderings of their new stadium, along with design studios Foster+Partners and Manica.

The timing of the event – which took place at the Sforzesco in the city centre – felt deliberate. Just two days before the derby, Milan and Inter got together to release the first images of how the new stadium will look.

Some details had been known for some time about the specifics of the project, but visualising it is another thing. Moreover, they dropped the bombshell before hand that a day one naming rights partner had been found: Generali, thus making it the Generali Stadium.

❗ OFFICIAL: How #ACMilan and Inter's new home the 'Generali Stadium' will look.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) October 29, 2026

Leaving aside any subjective thoughts on the design, it was a very proud moment for Cardinale. The American had made no secret of his desire to construct a new home for the two clubs, and he shed some light on things in an interview with CBS.

“You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

Something about the build-up to the derby, right up until kick-off, felt different. It seemed as though there was a conscious decision to try and create a connection with the past, something that Cardinale himself appeared to lead.

For example, Sky reported that Cardinale invited about 60 people to a dinner the night before the game. It wasn’t just an opportunity to catch up, but also for the American to explain what he has planned for Milan, seeking the support of some club legends.

The likes of Adriano Galliani, Ricardo Kaka and the Serie A president Simonelli attended the dinner. Other notable Milan legends present were Marcel Desailly, Serginho, Cristian Brocchi, Mathieu Flamini, Mauro Tassotti, Filippo Galli and Daniele Massaro.

At the Milan Store, racks of shirts adorned printing with names like Gattuso, Nesta, Seedorf, Inzaghi, Pirlo, Ambrosini, Kaka and even Maldini. The tag line behind the campaign was to ‘celebrate the heroes of Athens’, but again it felt like constructed timing.

Going back to that CBS interview, the bold proclamations that Cardinale made on the broadcast certainly turned some heads.

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this, don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved,” he said.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

Speaking of that link with the past, Kaka was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame. It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, while the Brazilian couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Those words might just have fallen very flat had Milan not delivered on the field, but they did. No doubt fired up by the emotionally-charged atmosphere inside the stadium, Gerry Cardinale got to watch on as his players delivered a show.

Diego Moreira – the man he reportedly pushed to sign personally for €51m – was the start of the show. He got two assists from Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot, two of his other favourites, before bending in a free-kick of his own. It was enough to blow the champions away.

Just 72 hours earlier, Cardinale had trudged through the mixed zone barely able to make eye contact with reporters after seeing his team implode against (at the time) bottom-half Bologna. On Halloween night, he had the smile of a child who had just scooped all the candy.

Speaking to QSVS, he got emotional: “What did you think of the boys? Every three days playing a game, going through the injuries, we get our full team back, and look at those guys. Those guys are winners. It brings tears to my eyes, it’s great right? The best night, and we’re going to build on this.”

🥲 “Look at those guys… it brings tears to my eyes.”

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 1, 2026

All of the pre-match hype, those ballsy interviews speaking of a desire to return to greatness, bringing legends back to invoke the nostalgia… it was a very risky move in hindsight. It could have backfired with a defeat, but the team delivered and gave everyone connected to the club immense pride.

So, within the space of four days and 180 minutes of football, Cardinale had witnessed both the floor and the ceiling of this team. The next mission – one he appears to be well aware of – is to bring the baseline up towards the obvious high potential Amorim’s group has.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport before the Inter game, the 59-year-old admitted that the squad is far from finished in his eyes, and that some further work is needed to try and get it up to the level required. He also invoked Top Gun to explain his bond with Amorim.

“We need to continue improving the squad because in the summer I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted. We’re rebuilding the team, and while I like the new arrivals, the ones who stayed, and the names I got rid of, it will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is to build a team that can deal with injuries. If you’re competing in European competitions and playing… Amorim Ball, which is high-tempo football, with quick transitions, where everyone runs between 9 and 11km per game, you have to rotate them.

“That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic in the January transfer market, and I’ll continue to strengthen our bench. My style is to move decisively and quickly.

“What matters to me is getting what we want, players… that are Milan-worthy. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to succeed.”

The first big step will be to welcome a very important jigsaw piece to complete the management puzzle: Markus Krösche. The past few days also seemed to serve to iron out the remaining details to reach an agreement with the German, who will become the new Head of Football.

You may wish to remain sceptical, and that is absolutely warranted, but for the first time in a while there does seem to be the semblance of a path out of the rut. A more active owner, a talented squad with room to improve, a coach being backed, a key director incoming and a new stadium on the way.

Oh, and of course the bragging rights, which are heading back across the Atlantic Ocean with Cardinale while he no doubt draws up the itinerary for his next visit.

#1476. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1475. Jack Grealish can't turn down a good night out and his attitude is a problem. IAN HERBERT reveals how the magnetic maverick star sparked concern and now faces a tragedy of missed opportunity

By IAN HERBERT, DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EDT, 2 November 2026

At the Pride of Britain awards a week back, we witnessed the brilliant and magnetic side of Jack Grealish, sprinkling stardust as he presented an award to a child of unimaginable courage who counts the Everton player as his hero. 'Footballers are classed as heroes – but these are the real heroes,' Grealish said that night. You could have heard a pin drop.

It was no different when he arrived back at Everton in September, to the delight of the kids awaiting him and his white Lamborghini in the country lane outside the club's Finch Farm training base. 'It feels so good. I think I'm at my best at everything in life when I feel loved,' Grealish said, articulating a very real sense that he was coming home.

He is popular around the club because it can be said without fear of exaggeration that he has a heart of gold.

Only on Thursday, an Everton-supporting father-of-three with a cancer diagnosis that gives him weeks to live disclosed that Grealish had put £10,000 his way. But within hours of that simple act of altruism coming to light, evidence of the other Grealish emerged, as Everton announced he had been excluded from the squad to face Newcastle in the Carabao Cup for failing to turn up for training last week.

It was by no means the first time. Everton sources say there had been similar causes for concern last season. Grealish reported sick ahead of last weekend's game at Arsenal, shortly after the Pride of Britain awards, and has breached Everton's disciplinary code through an unauthorised absence. The stated reason for his absence at Arsenal was illness.

Jack Grealish remains popular at Everton and has a heart of gold, shown by a £10,000 gift to a fan suffering from cancer, but he has since been dropped over a breach of discipline

There were similar causes for concern last season, with his return this summer going against David Moyes' better judgement

Everton's owners, looking for Grealish's glitz and glamour to gloss over their desperately poor and unambitious summer in the transfer window, were keen to bring him back. It was against David Moyes' own better judgement that he accepted his return as part of the deal that brought Iliman Ndiaye's unwelcome departure to Manchester City.

Moyes needed discipline in a thin squad where every player's contribution would count this season. It was an opportunity for the few star players to inspire and shine a light for the younger ones. And therein lies the tragedy of missed opportunity where Grealish is concerned.

He, the quintessential British maverick playmaker in the mould of George Best and Alan Hudson, could be a Goodison hero of these days, yet seems incapable of showing he is bothered, ridding himself of the acolytes and hangers on who are dragging him down, and appreciating what an opportunity football offers him.

Though he likes a drink, it's not so much booze as his attitude, and a struggle to turn down a good night out, which is contributing.

There is no doubt that he still has the skills to be a cherished player. That much was clear in the early stages of last season when he was providing more assists than any other Everton player until a broken foot requiring surgery brought a premature end to his season.

This season he has, as yet, no assists. He has perhaps been frustrated at the number of chances he has created not being converted, though not every winger has Erling Haaland as his support act.

Grealish's patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game, as he is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing

Look hard enough, though, and you'll see signs that his patchy attitude to a football life is affecting his game. He is not taking his man on in the way he used to and does not emit such light on the wing. Pep Guardiola, at Manchester City, was the first to see this and rapidly made it clear he wanted him gone.

It's not too late for the 31-year-old to become the totemic presence that so many fervently want him to be on Merseyside. Moyes, who sees the wasted potential, has given him abundant support and patience since City left him out in the cold, hoping that he can make him see the opportunity, here.

Thursday night's excellent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United opens up the potential for an exciting Cup run, with Fleetwood Town awaiting in the quarter-finals. Everton have not won a trophy for 31 years.

The hope must be that the significantly public nature of Grealish's omission – very much a case of Moyes refusing to tolerate another breach – will shock him into action.

It was even the wish of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, present at Thursday night's match, that Grealish would be re-signed to Everton and the PM declared after meeting him at the Pride of Britain awards that the player was an example of the way people 'buy into Everton.'

The collective wish for him to thrive at the club could not be clearer. Only he can make that happen.

#1474. Spitting row mars feisty Millwall-West Ham clash

A spitting row marred the 100th Millwall-West Ham United derby and first for 14 years.

Taty Castellanos was facing trial by video after being accused of spitting on Filip Marschall during Saturday’s febrile 2-2 draw at the Den.

Millwall goalkeeper Marschall made the allegation to referee Paul Tierney, who was expected to include it in an official report that would then be assessed by the Football Association.

Spitting on an opponent is punishable with a six-match ban.

Telegraph Sport has been told West Ham striker Castellanos denies he spat on Marschall and believes he will be vindicated by video footage of the incident.

Lying little prick. Taty didn't spit ❌ pic.twitter.com/5vYxOtKqof

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

“I’d be extremely surprised if Fil’s made an accusation and nothing’s happened. But that’s not really for me to deal with; I’m sure the authorities will deal with that.”

West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo said: “I’m aware of the allegation. I didn’t see the image; I didn’t speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that.”

He added: “I’m going to try to look at the images.”

There were also ugly scenes at full time when players had to be separated at the end of a derby that had been at the centre of an unprecedented police operation.

There were six arrests as of 4pm on Saturday for offences including tailgating, assault on a police officer and entering or attempting to enter a stadium while intoxicated.

Eleven men were also arrested at around 7.15pm on Friday on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage.

The group, believed to be Millwall fans, were detained in the vicinity of a known West Ham supporters’ pub in Stratford.

Saturday’s fixture was subject to a five-mile dispersal zone, the largest ever for a football match in London, with officers granted special powers to stop and search people and vehicles without reasonable suspicion and to remove anyone causing disorder.

Riot police were out in force outside the ground, with dog units and mounted officers among 400 personnel deployed – roughly quadruple the usual number for a game there.

Those and other measures – including the use of live facial recognition, a strict segregation policy and a 12.30pm kick-off to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time – prevented a repeat of the kind of violence which has marred this fixture down the years.

West Ham fans also received a police escort to a game that saw both sets of supporters hurl foul-mouthed insults at each other throughout.

Plans to keep rival spectators apart after the match were reportedly tested by scuffles that broke out as people left the ground.

If the police were ready for a fight before the game, West Ham’s players were not as Millwall tore into them from the first whistle and dominated a first half in which they scored twice through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli and hit the crossbar through a stunning 35-yard strike by Mark Sykes.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

However, the Championship leaders finally turned up in the second half and pulled a goal back through Mohamadou Kanté before Konstantinos Mavropanos equalised with just 10 minutes to go.

ALL SQUARE at the Den 🙌West Ham equalise in the 80th minute.Everything to play for with just 10 minutes remaining 👀 pic.twitter.com/qQmDlyuQmT

That was only after Marschall gestured that he had been spat at by Castellanos following a melee in the penalty area.

Tierney did, though, brandish a red card when Kanté pulled back Kyrell Lisbie as the substitute robbed him of the ball on the halfway line and ran clean through on goal.

The foul denied Lisbie the chance to hand Millwall their first win over their bitter rivals for 22 years, much to the frustration of fans who had roared them on from first whistle to last.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Describing the atmosphere as “absolutely the best by far” since he joined the club almost two years ago, Neil said: “I told the players prior to the game that this game’s a real rarity and, as a player and as a manager, it’s a privilege to be part of it.”

Millwall: Marschall; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Sturge; Metcalfe (Servais 81), Mazou-Sacko (Cundle 90); Sykes (Baggott 70), Dykes, Neghli; Arconte (Lisbie 81).Booked: Lisbie 90+5.Goals: Taylor 16, Neghli 45+3.Subs not used: Batth, Crocombe, Doughty, Issoufou, Kelly.West Ham United: Hermansen; Walker-Peters (Kanté 46), Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa (Austbo 68), Solomon; Piroe (Pablo 46), Castellanos (Orford 90).Booked: Morato 40, Pablo 83, Kilman 86, Mavropanos 90+5.Sent off: Kanté 89.Goals: Kanté 74, Mavropanos 80.Subs not used: Ajala, Austbo, Golambeckis, Herrick, Magassa, Scarles.Referee: Paul Tierney.

🗣️ "We started to tire in the second half"Millwall manager Alex Neil shares his thoughts on this afternoon's Dockers Derby, after the Lions drew 2-2 with West Ham. pic.twitter.com/xnmubZ9NIz

🗣️ 'We were able to bounce back, but we need to look at the things we have not done so well'Nuno Espirito Santo reflects on West Ham's performance after the Hammers fought back from 2-0 down to draw with Millwall. pic.twitter.com/NM1wQVcN0o

Asked by Sky Sports for his view on the “spitting” incident, Alex Neil said: “Fil [Marschall] was saying to the referee throughout the game when that happened at that point... “I’m sure the referee and authorities who need to deal with it will look at it and, if it warrants it, it needs dealt with and then I’m sure they will.”

Will there be one final chance? Sturge earns a throw-in on the far side and Dykes limbers up... But West Ham clear their lines and that is that. It ends two goals apiece.

Lisbie has looked dangerous down that left side and he just runs out of room under pressure from Mavropanos. The pair square up, with Lisbie sticking his finger into the Greek’s cheek.

Lisbie darts to the by-line but his cutback does not make it through the thicket of limbs and West Ham clear their lines.

Millwall earn a free-kick to the left of the box as Mavropanos climbs all over Dykes. Servais picks out Baggott at the far post and his knock-down lands to Dykes who, will spinning, strikes the ball over the bar.

DYKES! 😱So close to a late winner for Millwall, but his shot flies over the bar. pic.twitter.com/fQFpQBdS7j

Neghli steps up to take it but it strikes the wall.

There will be five minutes of time added on...

Woah.. Kante gets his pocket picked by Lisbie on the half-way line and the West Ham goalscorer has no choice but to foul him as the last man. West Ham have a free-kick just outside the box.

RED CARD 🟥West Ham are down to ten men, after Kante was sent off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity. pic.twitter.com/jRlVwLNiOs

Millwall have put so much into this and it’s starting to tell. Their players look leggy and aren’t able to track Kante’s run into the channel though Cooper is just about able to clear his lines. Bowen’s corner comes to nothing.

Pablo’s at it again, steaming his way into the left half-space, but Mazou-Sacko does well to track back and block the Brazilian’s effort. The resulting corner is gathered by Marschall who attempts to send Servais away but Kilman is wise to it and takes a booking for a professional foul.

Mazou-Sacko has his hands all over Pablo’s back and while the Brazilian is awarded a free-kick he slams the ball to the ground feeling he had broken free. He earns a booking for his troubles and the resulting free-kick comes to nothing.

It’s Bowen’s turn to try an effort at goal. Metcalfe does brilliantly to charge it down but there is no respite for Millwall as Kante’s long-range sighter goes behind for another corner.

That goal has changed the dynamic of this match. Millwall have dropped into a back five and West Ham are all over them. Bowen earns his side a corner and his delivery comes out to Solomon on the edge of the box, and while Cooper is able to partially clear, Austbo stings the gloves of Marschall from distance to win another corner.

Millwall 2 West Ham 1 (Kante) The substitute strokes a right-footed effort into the bottom corner from outside the box. A great finish.

The versatile defender Baggott is on for Sykes. ITV have just shown a replay of the “spitting” incident but it’s really difficult to make anything out from that distance.

The resulting corner comes to nothing. ITV are relaying reports of a counter-claim from Millwall that Castellanos might have spat in Marschall’s direction.

Chance! Bowen stands up a delightful cross and Pablo forces Marschall into a fine stop. Corner awarded.

Some confusion here as Marschall appears to have taken too long over a goal-kick, and while most believe that a West Ham corner had been awarded, it ends up being a goal-kick.

The ITV commentators say that West Ham are alleging that Marschall spat in Pablo’s direction.

Arconte chases down a lost cause and telescopes a leg through Taylor to earn a corner. He spins around to the home supporters and windmills his arms in their direction as the volume increases. Metcalfe’s cross is well overhit, though, and sails out for a goal-kick.

Kante’s runs in behind are threatening to disrupt Millwall’s backline shape, but Neil’s midfield sentries Mazou-Sacko and Metcalfe are doing such a great job to cover the gaps that the hosts still look like they have things under control.

A thunderous chant of “Milllllllll” echoes around the ground as the home fans spur their charges on.

Oof. Metcalfe leaves a foot in on Morato, his studs going into the defender’s Achilles. He should perhaps consider himself lucky to avoid punishment there. One that VAR may have intervened on in the Premier League.

Penalty shout! Metcalfe drives forward into the right of the box and Kante, who is hot pursuit, pushes the midfielder to the ground. Tierney immediately waves away the appeals and replays concur that the contact is probably not strong enough to warrant a penalty.

Bowen is presented with some grass to run into but his cross is well cleared. He gets another bite at the cherry, trying his luck from the edge of the box and Marschall just about gets to the rebound ahead of an onrushing Kante. A corner is awarded which the Millwall stopper flaps at but his team-mates are able to avert the danger.

West Ham earn a chance to deliver a corner from the near side but Engel’s inswinger finds Marschall’s gloves. Really poor.

Millwall continue leveraging Cooper and Taylor’s height in the box off set-pieces. Here, Metcalfe’s free-kick skims off the top of Cooper’s head but just misses the mark.

It looks like West Ham have gone to three at the back as Kante joins Mukasa and Engels in midfield. He’ll look to make late runs in behind.

Entering the West Ham box, he attempts to hold off Cooper but Osei-Tutu snaps in and earns a free-kick.

Two changes from Nuno, who takes off Piroe and Walker-Peters for Pablo and Kante.

Millwall have been good value for their lead, taking 16 shots and creating three big chances. West Ham, conversely have managed just one shot, off-target, despite controlling two-thirds of possession.

Arne Engel’s heatmap suggests he’s spent most of the match inside or just in advance of West Ham’s defensive third, which is not where Nuno will want either him or Divine Mukasa. The West Ham head coach could be tempted into changes at the break.

This is no more than Millwall – and West Ham – deserve. Sykes’s outrageous 35-yard strike deserved a goal and Neghli makes sure justice is served on the stroke of half-time. The roar that greets the players leaving the field is deafening.

The Den is in dreamland. Millwall take a two-goal advantage into the break and Neil celebrates with unbridled delight on the touchline. A caveat, though... Millwall did spurn a 2-0 lead in their most recent match away at Middlesbrough.

Millwall 2 West Ham 0 (Neghli) It’s come from yet another Dykes long throw, which West Ham have failed to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Neghli in the six-yard box and he spears the ball beyond Hermansen and Bowen on the line. And that’s the half.

"It's DREAMLAND at the Den!!"🫶🏼Millwall snatch a second goal before the break, as Neghli drills it home.An unbelievable half from the home side. pic.twitter.com/NIfSmwkHXh

Chance! Sykes from 30 yards strikes the ball cleanly and his ferocious effort beats Hermansen all ends up but ricochets off the woodwork and away to safety. Two minutes of time added on, by the way...

WHAT A HIT!! 💥Sykes' long-range effort RATTLES the crossbar. A potential contender for goal of the season, had that gone into the net... pic.twitter.com/ivBOslIZaO

Millwall, for the umpteenth time, find themselves in a two-vs-two situation on the beak, as Arconte tries to twist Kilman one way and then the other. He sets the ball to Metcalfe but the contact is not great and Hermansen gathers.

West Ham threaten Millwall’s lead momentarily as Mukasa breaks down their right, but Marschall does well to smother the ball and earns a free-kick on the process.

There’s a muted appeal for a penalty as Mavropanos nudges Cooper to the floor, but it’s a soft contact which takes place outside of the box anyhow.

Castellanos then attempts to burst down the right but Mazou-Sacko, who has been fantastic thus far, steams in and boots the ball out of play before geeing up the crowd.

Another foul... Osei-Tutu jumps into Morato but West Ham give the free-kick straight back to their opponents.

Morato leaves a leg in as Osei-Tutu attempts to break free, perhaps in retaliation to the earlier discretion, and he earns the first booking of the match.

It’s seven-seven in the fouls contest for those wondering, the latest being a mistimed challenge on Sykes by Castellanos near the right touchline. Millwall pump another ball into the box which is not up to much.

In an attempt to get his foot on the ball, Engels has often peeled out to the right-back position, but a wild, desperate cross-field ball that goes straight to Osei-Tutu sums up West Ham’s half aptly.

A wild challenge from Metcalfe on Cooper earns West Ham a free-kick and its then Sykes’ turn to land a late tackle, this time in the right channel. The subsequent delivery finds Castellanos but he cannot direct the ball goalwards.

West Ham’s strength comes from the fluidity of their front four, but Nuno’s creators have not been able to access them. So effective has Millwall’s back-line coverage been that West Ham have only managed low-quality final-third entries.

For the first time this half, Millwall begin to retreat deep into their own half, their lines of defence merging. And while West Ham tot up a fair number of passes on the edge of the box, they ultimately cede possession and Millwall spring a counter. Arconte appears to be through but Kilman does well to recover and Dykes’ subsequent shot is charged down.

West Ham are not learning their lessons and Sturge almost pulls off a similar pass in behind for Arconte, but the linesman raises his flag on this occasion. Replays show that it was really tight.

Millwall are going man-to-man as West Ham try to build and the visitors are struggling to get out. Sturge works infield from his starting perch on the left and almost threads a through-ball in behind for Arconte to gallop on to but Kilman does well to stick in a boot.

West Ham are desperately trying to calm this game down, but the Millwall fans are making that quite the challenge. The visitors string a series of passes together before Bowen strays offside.

Millwall then burst forward, Arconte this time popping up in a dangerous position on the right but Metcalfe fires over having picked off a loose Hammers pass out from the back.

Another Dykes throw-in sparks panic in West Ham’s box. Osei-Tutu’s back-post header appears to take a deflection off Walker-Peters, but the referee awards a goal-kick.

Millwall 1 West Ham 0 (Taylor) If at first you don’t succeed, try and try again... Dykes’ long throw from the right prompts chaos on the West Ham box and although Hermansen is able to keep out efforts from Sykes and Arconte, he can’t deny Taylor from close range. Cue bedlam in the stands. A massive, massive goal.

Or not… The Den erupts! That was appalling defending from a long throw and West Ham got exactly what they deserved, with Mads Hemansen’s brilliant save failing to spare them.

MILLWALL STRIKE FIRST 🔥Caleb Taylor fires the Lions in front! pic.twitter.com/pPffYZD73D

It is all Millwall so far. They have been first to pretty much every ball and are giving West Ham no time on it at all. Konstantinos Mavropanos has just bought the visitors a breather after going down injured.

Hermansen gets caught in no-man’s land as Millwall spin in another ball from deep. It falls to the feet of Dykes but his effort does not have the requisite power to beat Kilman on the line.

Mavropanos appears to have been taken out by his own goalkeeper in the commotion and receives some on-field medical treatment.

Neil will be happy with how his side have started this match. Their intensity off the ball has forced West Ham into errors and here Sturge picks Bowen’s pocket on the halfway line before picking out Arconte in the box. He tries to squeeze a shot through Mukasa but the young midfielder does well to clear his lines.

The resulting corner comes out to Mazou-Sacko on the edge of the box but his effort sails over the bar.

Dykes and Arconte are Millwall’s attacking threats and the former wins a free-kick in the left channel. The hosts load the box with their biggest aerial threats but Metcalfe’s teasing inswinger just evades everyone. Tierney blows up for a foul anyhow...

There’s a minor clash off the ball as Morato and Cooper exchange words. Paul Tierney speaks with both players before Dykes launches a long throw into the box which is cleared and Hermansen is wise to the subsequent cross off the second phase.

Arconte tiptoes into the West Ham box and picks out Sturge whose miscued shot finds Metcalfe on the edge of the box. His effort is straight at Hermansen who collects the ball calmly.

That Jenson Metcalfe tackle on West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen came after just 15 seconds. What Vinny Jones might call “a reducer”.

"That's the expectation, I would imagine" 😅The first free-kick is awarded just 12 seconds into Millwall's derby against West Ham.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/qpxjQEKN6x

Millwall launch a free-kick from deep into the box after Castellanos gives away a needless foul and after some pinball Hermansen gathers.

It took just 13 seconds for us to get our first foul. Kudos to anyone who had that in their Dockers Derby sweepstake... A late lunge from Metcalfe on Bowen.

And the players emerge, Hey Jude now being played... Millwall are in their customary navy-blue home strip and white shorts. West Ham are giving their new white away kit a first outing.

There’s just about enough time for the two sides to meet for quick summits before Millwall get us under way!

The atmosphere is building nicely in the ground and the players are now lined up in the tunnel, Cooper and Bowen standing shoulder to shoulder.

Seats are filling up rapidly with barely 10 minutes before kick-off, with the away end a notable exception. The home fans are making their own presence felt as The Jam’s A Town Called Malice and The Clash’s London Calling blare out over the public-address system.

"The fans are up for it, the players are up for it" 💪🏼Lyndon Dykes looks ahead to today's match, and reflects on his strong start to life as a Millwall player.Watch it LIVE on ITV1 🎥 pic.twitter.com/V9nPzbh3Ob

Kevin Nolan, West Ham’s captain, was sent off early but his team-mates defied the odds to win 2-1 thanks to goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid either side of a stunning Liam Trotter strike.

In Millwall’s match-day squad that day were… Harry Kane and Ryan Mason.

The last time West Ham and Millwall met, Harry Kane was a Millwall player 😅This is how that game in 2012 played out 👇 pic.twitter.com/OhtVx3caCP

This rivalry was forged in different circumstances from most derby confrontations. There is none of the religious divide of Celtic and Rangers, or the politics of Barcelona against Real Madrid, or the spat over title-winning superiority of Manchester United and Liverpool. This is a tale of proximity, an internecine feud.

“There’s no politics, no nationality, nothing like that,” says Nick Hart, who hosts the weekly podcast Achtung! Millwall. “We’re very similar people, from the same backgrounds, same communities. But it’s in the Millwall supporter’s DNA for West Ham to be the ultimate rivals. Nobody else comes into the equation. You’re brought up on this stuff. It’s your history.”

Though possibly more recent history than might be suggested by the two clubs’ early foundations. The hostility that West Ham will face at the Den is no more about dockland rivalry, north-south London disputes or strike-breaking than the animosity when Manchester United visit Anfield is caused by the building of the Manchester Ship Canal.

“It really is about the hooligan era,” says a podcaster who uses the pseudonym Former West Ham Employee on the West Ham Way podcast. “The two clubs had notorious fanbases. And they grated. It came about through vying to be the No 1, battling to see who had the hardest mob. Whenever we’ve played – or even been in close proximity – things have happened.”

Jake Cooper on making the 500th appearance of his career against West Ham today! 👏Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/lTzXOwXhxd

There have only been 18 meetings between these fierce rivals since the Second World War, but absence has certainly not made the heart grow fonder. Here are some of the feud’s most notable flashpoints.

At the 1972 testimonial in honour of Harry Cripps – the renowned Millwall hard man – police horses were sent on to the pitch after West Ham supporters entered the home section at The Den. Fighting spilt over into the streets surrounding the ground.

An even bleaker turn came in 1976, when Millwall fan Ian Pratt died in a skirmish with West Ham fans at New Cross station that led to his fall under a train.

Leaflets were later handed out in the Den’s Cold Blow Lane end with a grainy picture of Pratt and a declaration in capital letters: “A West Ham fan must die next week to avenge him.”

Millwall plundered four goals on Mothering Sunday in 2004 as Tim Cahill’s double helped them to a 4-1 victory over West Ham at the Den in an incident-filled derby.

The hosts missed a penalty and had another saved by Stephen Bywater, who was later sent off. Violence followed in the stands and the match was named “The Mothers’ Day Massacre”.

Mother's Day Massacre ⏮️A 4-1 victory over The Hammers back in 2004. pic.twitter.com/TLi7xkcVJG

A hundred West Ham and Millwall supporters clashed during a screening of England’s 2006 World Cup match against Paraguay in Canada Square, which led to 16 injuries and one hospitalisation.

The clubs’ League Cup meeting in 2009 at Upton Park was listed as Category Five by police, the most serious risk of violence, and resulted in a Millwall supporter being stabbed in Priory Road, near the ground.

The Metropolitan Police said that “planned” scuffles, which involved more than 100 fans, appeared to have been caused by fans without tickets to the game.

Just spotted one Millwall fan outside the ground in blue boxing gloves. He is also wearing what appear to be slippers, so not sure what that means…

Nuno Espirito Santo has only been through the door at West Ham for a matter of months, but he insisted he is fully aware of the significance of today’s fixture.

When asked about his perception of the rivalry, Nuno said: “Since the fixture list came out, this date has been [important], for both of the clubs. It’s special, special game. We look forward to go and compete against a good team.

“It’s a different game from all of the other games, it’s a special game, the atmosphere will be different… Steve [Potts, first-team coach and former West Ham player] has been involved in many of these games, he’s constantly speaking about how special it is for West Ham fans, so we have a lot of information and we are fully aware of the importance of the game.

On potential unrest between fans and the significant police presence, Nuno added: “What we want most is that everything goes well, both fans supporting their teams and no conflict. We have people inside the club who are taking care of that. We have to focus on our tasks.”

The gaffer on tomorrow's fixture ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/6NG6t4t4Fn

#westham on the way to #millwall via #london bridge #whufc #coyi pic.twitter.com/HrWgJ6UtJY

Riot police are very much out in force outside The Den today for the 100th competitive derby between Millwall and West Ham United and first for 14 years. Dog units and mounted officers can been seen patrolling the perimeter of the ground, with 400 personnel deployed to stop violence erupting between rival fans – roughly quadruple the usual number for a fixture here. There has been no sign of any trouble with less than an hour to go before kick-off.

The game has been scheduled for 12.30pm to minimise supporters’ pre-match drinking time, although plenty of fans have been nursing pints before entering the ground. Other measures in place include the use of live facial recognition cameras, while a dispersal order has been imposed covering a large area around the stadium. Police were also planning to escort West Ham fans from South Bermondsey station, which will also be closed to home supporters for up to an hour after full-time. The latter measure has been deemed safer than holding the 1,800 away fans back following the game.

The Millwall-West Ham derby is one of the most notorious in English football and was most recently marred by serious violence when the sides met at Upton Park for a League Cup tie back in 2009. One man was stabbed and the match itself was interrupted on three occasions by fans invading the pitch.

Alex Neil switches out goalkeeper Max Crocombe for Filip Marschall and names the returning Mathis Servais, Kyrell Lisbie and Alfie Doughty on the bench.

Alex Neil names his Lions XI 👊 pic.twitter.com/MP0N9wMatG

Just the one change from the league leaders’ last league match as Kyle Walker-Peters comes in for the injured Joel Veltman.

Today's teamsheet 📋 pic.twitter.com/EmrxYRhsPd

"We have to quiet them down" 🤫West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen is expecting a hostile atmosphere at The Den today 🗣️Watch all the action with NOW! https://t.co/56JOZ0NPsr pic.twitter.com/9tp2225Rq8

The Metropolitan Police will have 400 officers on the streets of east London for this match – about four times the norm for a Championship fixture – and it has enforced a Section 35 dispersal order in the area highlighted on the map below.

A Section 35 order authorises a Police Constable and a Police Community Support Officer in uniform to “exclude a person from an area for a period of up to 48 hours with an Inspector’s authority”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the highly anticipated Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United as the two clubs meet officially for the 100th time. This fixture has not been staged since 2012, and the intervening 14 years have done little to temper the ill-feeling between their passionate supporters, who will be anxious to claim bragging rights over their Dockers Derby rivals. The Metropolitan Police have placed a Section 35 dispersal order in the area surrounding The Den and will deploy 400 officers on the streets of east London.

Acrimony between the two clubs has existed since the late 19th century when Millwall Athletic, originally Rovers, battled it out against Thames Ironworks, later renamed West Ham at the Athletic and Memorial Grounds. Sixty of the two clubs’ 99 meetings came between 1899 and 1915, and while they played just seven times between 1946 and 1987, the irregularity of the game only added to its mystique, which has often spilt over into the ugly.

Both head coaches spoke at length about the significance of today’s match, with Alex Neil, in the Millwall dugout, describing it as an encounter that means “absolutely everything” but imploring his players to keep “cool heads”. His counterpart Nuno Espírito Santo revealed that he had been well advised about the game’s importance by Steve Potts, his first-team coach and former West Ham player.

Since the club’s last meeting in 2012, West Ham have ascended into the Premier League, moved into the London Stadium and won the Uefa Conference League, only falling back into England’s second tier last summer where Millwall have remained for all but two seasons. The Lions brushed maddeningly close to promotion in their last campaign as they pushed for an automatic spot until the very last weekend of the regular season before falling to Hull City in the play-off semi-finals.

Much of the pre-match talk will centre on the clubs’ long-standing rivalry, but beneath the bile and belligerence is an intriguing football match between two sides. Millwall are missing 11 first-team players and face the daunting task of stopping a West Ham side who have found their feet in the Championship, scoring 16 goals in their last four league matches.

#1473. McKennie ruled out of AZ trip with adductor fatigue as Alajbegović and Cabal return

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

A short rest should be enough, because the injury is fatigue rather than a tear, Sky Sport Italia reported. He should be back for the league. The problem is in his right adductor. The medical staff will check him again before Thursday, ANSA said.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. At 19 years and 41 days, the teenager has set a new mark: no non-Italian scorer in a Serie A meeting of these two clubs has been younger.

His knee knock has already cleared up. Cabal made way for Andrea Cambiaso after 83 minutes with cramp. That is put down to him not having started a game for some time. He will be available in Alkmaar.

Their return matters because the squad is badly stretched. Seven players are on the long-term injury list. Rugani, Zhegrova, Ekhator and Milik were left out of the UEFA squad. Losing McKennie, who can play several positions, leaves Spalletti with even fewer options for the trip to the Netherlands.

The match at AZ kicks off at 21:00 CET on 5 November. It is Matchday 4 of the league phase. Juventus have two wins and a draw so far.

AZ will be hard to break down at home. Their last home defeat in Europe was 4-1 to Aston Villa in the Conference League in October 2023.

Juventus arrive in good scoring form. They have nine goals in this season’s Europa League. Only Benfica, with ten, have scored more. That is Juventus’s best total after three games of a European campaign since 1999/2000.

⚪⚫ Kerim Alajbegović's first league goal for Juventus ✅#UEL | @juventusfc pic.twitter.com/GPcn8KJZga

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) November 2, 2026

History against Dutch opposition also offers encouragement. Juventus are unbeaten in three previous Europa League games against Dutch clubs, with two wins and one draw. They scored seven goals and conceded one in those matches.

McKennie’s absence will shape the midfield in Alkmaar, but the focus will quickly shift to his recovery. His place for the next league game is in doubt. Juventus visit Fiorentina on Matchday 11, on Sunday 8 November 2026 at 20:45.

#1472. It’s official for Cristiano Ronaldo Junior

Would Cristiano Ronaldo’s rant have paid off? A month after showing his dissatisfaction at not seeing his young boy summoned to the Portugal U17s, according to Recordthe star striker of Al-Nassr (41 years old) can have a smile.

“Cristianinho” figures well in the list of Seleçao nuggets who will play in the qualifications for the next Under-17 Euro. Coach Filipe Ramos selected the striker among the 23 players summoned for this gathering. A big first for him.

Aged 16, Cristiano Junior made his debut for Portugal in May 2025 and already has 13 caps, with the U15s (4 matches) then the U16s (9 matches). Author of 5 goals, the eldest son of “CR7” is the pride of his five-time Ballon d’Or father.

While he usually plays in Saudi Arabia, among the young people of Cristiano Ronaldo’s club, this call-up will give him additional exposure. The Portuguese U17s will face Andorra (November 11), Bulgaria (November 14) and Serbia (November 17).

#1471. Bundesliga: Leipzig continues, Friborg revives, spectacular victory for Stuttgart in Leverkusen

The 8th day of the Bundesliga offered several notable results this Saturday. The big surprise came from Stuttgart, who scored a spectacular victory on the lawn of Bayer Leverkusen (4-2). RB Leipzig also carried out a great operation by winning at Schalke 04 (2-0), confirming its ambitions at the top of the ranking. For its part, Friborg went to get three precious points in Augsburg (2-1), while Werder Bremen dominated Hoffenheim (2-0). Finally, Borussia Mönchengladbach and Paderborn parted with a goalless draw (0-0).

A particularly favorable day for Stuttgart and Leipzig, who left their mark on the outside. Bayer Leverkusen, on the other hand, let important points slip away after an insufficient defensive performance. All eyes are now on the poster for the evening between Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. This Klassiker promises to be decisive in the race for first places and could reshuffle the cards at the top of the Bundesliga.
