It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it quickly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Secret to Harry Kane’s England longevity? ‘He strikes the ball better than Ronaldo’

Right foot, goal. Left foot, goal. Edge of the area, goal. Inside the area, goal. Under pressure, goal, Right foot, save. Left foot, goal. That was Harry Kane’s warm-up prior to England’s 7-0 demolition of Croatia and it underlined just why the striker will equal Peter Shilton’s appearance record on Tuesday night.

As demonstrated in Rijeka, Kane’s career has been a non-stop pursuit of excellence that has led him to the very top of the national game. England’s record goalscorer will also become the joint most-capped player with Shilton, when he makes his 125th appearance against the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday night.

Eberechi Eze is set to start for England in the clash against Czech Republic tonight. The Arsenal forward is poised to come in for Anthony Gordon, who has started in the three matches during the Nations League international break. Trent Alexander-Arnold is also due to play at right-back, with Jarell Quansah moving to centre-back to cover for Ezri Konsa.

Alex Scott has been ruled out through injury, which has upset Bournemouth after he played in the win over Croatia at the weekend. Myles Lewis-Skelly is expected to get a recall to the team after playing against Czech Republic in Prague last week when England won 2-0. Morgan Rogers, who scored against Croatia, is in line to start in place of Bukayo Saka.

Probable England team: Pickford; Trent, Quansah, Guehi, Hall; Lewis-Skelly, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham, Eze; Kane

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

#1420. Cristiano Ronaldo is left out of Al-Nassr match due to 'security concerns' as countryman Joao Felix stars in his absence

By PRESS ASSOCIATION and HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 11:37 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 14:01 EDT, 2 November 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo did not travel for Al-Nassr's AFC Champions League fixture against Pakhtakor on Monday amid ongoing security concerns.

The 41-year-old Portugal star was among a number of players left out by coach Ange Postecoglou for the trip to Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

In Ronaldo's absence, fellow Portugal international Joao Felix netted a brace in a momentous 6-2 win for Postecoglou's side.

The Australian coach also rested Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan, telling a news conference he had made the decision 'given the pressure of matches and the amount of travel involved'.

It came a week after Al Nassr's match at home to Al Wasl was postponed, with the UAE club refusing to travel due to the situation in Saudi Arabia.

Airports in the country have come under a series of attacks undertaken by Houthi rebels.

Cristiano Ronaldo was rested from Al-Nassr's clash with Pakhtakor due to security concerns

Operating with backing from Tehran, the Houthis are seeking to disrupt Saudi Arabia's oil exports. One recent attack from the militants killed 13 people.

Last week Ronaldo scored a hat-trick against Al Kholood in the Saudi Pro League on Thursday, taking him to nine goals in 12 appearances this season.

Ronaldo's treble has taken him to 985 career goals as he edges nail-bitingly close to the ultimate milestone that he has been chasing for many years, since breaking the record for top goalscorer in football history in 2021.

Addressing the target with his former team-mate Rio Ferdinand in 2024, Ronaldo said: 'I want to reach 1,000 goals. If I don't have any injuries, this for me is the most important (thing), I want that.

'For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.'

Despite surpassing Josef Bican five years ago as the all-time top goalscorer for club and country, that number is contested due to a lack of data from some historical records.

Last month, Ronaldo became football's first multi-billionaire after the veteran forward raked in £225million this year, according to Forbes.

Ronaldo reportedly passed the $2billion mark in career earnings earlier this year, just six years after he was the first footballer to surpass $1billion.

Ronaldo's status comes as he again topped Forbes' football rich list, aided by a lucrative salary at Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr which is estimated at £488,000-per-day.

Forbes has determined that Ronaldo has also earned £42million off the pitch over the course of the year, which has come via endorsements and his business ventures.

Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.

When you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

We brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

Unbelievable. Against Brighton we were not at the level. This was all about bouncing back. This is my first official game at home. Great finish, I am very happy. My job if on the bench is to give a headache to the manager.

I have been proving myself in the Premier League but it was important for me today.

Leeds have a great team, a top game. Glad we could get the three points.

A game of three thirds, two of them with Leeds in the ascendancy, the last with Arsenal showing their class and wealth. The winning goal was glorious but Leeds, who have lost their unbeaten record, were impressive.

Gabriel gets his head on a couple of crosses, knocking the second of them away from Calvert-Lewin.

Saka, with the last kick of the game, and through one one one with Trafford, shoots into the stands.

Ampadu’s long throw is headed away by Bruno and on by Merino who knocks it safe and out of play.

Trafford comes 20 yards out of his box to try to keep Leeds going but miscontrols with his chest. Gyokeres takes it round him and has an open goal but checks and goes wider and Leeds manage to move enough bodies back to thwart him.

Five minutes of stoppage time are signalled. Ally McCoist names the substitute Bruno as the man of the match. He was certainly the catalyst for a revival.

Odegaard had just fizzed a cute pass to Bruno in the left of the Leeds box but he couldn’t control it.

Calvert-Lewin is played in over the top and squares for Aaronson to shoot into a defender. He would have been better off leaving it for Nmecha.

Fair to say Leeds were the better side for an hour but have suffered a slow puncture since the equaliser.

Odegaard is booked for delaying Leeds’ goal-kick.

Odegaard misses an open goal, flicking his finish to Trafford after two brilliant touches from Rice to trap a deep cross from the left and roll it across the six-yard box.

Bruno Guimarães has now scored two goals for Arsenal and they have both been beauties. The first was a long-range screamer at Sunderland and this was more of a team effort. Saka to Odegaard, Odegaard to Rice, Rice to Bruno. Gorgeous football. The first time Arsenal have produced such a move all afternoon.

Aaronson does well to get back and block Saka’s shot after being put through by Bruno’s sharp pass.

The difference between the two sides today has been the ability to throw £50m players on off the bench.

After some confusion as the fourth official initially put up Gudmundsson’s number.

Rice heads the cross away and Justin clips Bruno’s heels to thwart a counter and becomes the fifth Leeds booking.

Leeds are readying Nmecha as Gudmundsson’s direct running earns them a free-kick on the left. Eight Leeds players go into the box.

Arsenal are now pouring forward in numbers, and with the swagger of champions. Saka blazes over from 20 yards after being set up by Timber’s run.

Nothing much Leeds could have done to defend that goal.

Arsenal 2 Leeds 1 (Bruno) Fine goal. Odegaard pings a pass into the area, Rice backheels it and Bruno, who started the move by nutmegging Tanaka, whips the ball into the bottom left corner.

You wouldn’t say that equaliser was coming but that’s the thing about Calafiori: the Italian is capable of producing the unpredictable. He now has five goal involvements (three goals, two assists) in 10 appearances this season for club and country.

Arsenal have a second corner in a minute after Muhareemovic heads Odegaard’s cross behind. Calvert-Lewin heads it away at the near post, Saka shifts it into the middle and Calafiori runs on to smash a shot wide from 20 yards.

After tearing a hole in Arsenal’s defence down the left to score, they do so on the other side with Bogle who bends a wonderful pass through the six-yard box and Calvert-Lewin slides in at the back post. Longer studs and he would have scored.

Arsenal 0 Leeds 1 (Justin) Fully deserved. Finishes with a right-foot shot at the back post after Okafor sent Gudmundsson in behind White and the left-back galloped on to it and set up the marauding centre-half perfectly. Fine finish too.

The Arsenal fans were becoming increasingly agitated a few minutes before that opening goal. They can see that Leeds have been setting traps and that Arsenal are falling into those traps. James Justin gives Leeds a deserved lead.

Raya turns Tanaka’s blistering, swerving effort over the bar and Leeds are penalised at the corner again. Justin, moments earlier, had rifled a shot over and Leeds are swarming all over Arsenal.

Odegaard shoots from the 18-yard line after being set up by the good combination play ofCcalafiori and Madueke down the left but sweeps his tame daisycutter easily within Trafford’s reachh.

Saka heads Madueke’s left-wing cross on to the roof of the net when trying to direct it back into the middle.

Arsenal fans must be thinking this is a job for the box-crasher himself, Mikel Merino.

Leeds squeeze Arsenal’s attack again and the ball runs out for a goalkick after Odegaard’s attempt to free White down the right fails.

No changes. Tanaka needs to be more discreet this half if he is to avoid a second yellow card. Arsenal attack quickly down the right buy Muharemovic sticks with Saka all the way to usher the ball out for a goalkick.

8 - Arsenal (5) and Leeds United (3) recorded eight offsides in total in the first half, the most in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League game since Manchester United v Aston Villa in April 2023 (also 8). Lines. https://t.co/er4wTVAIJS

Arteta just wrote a few notes on the little notepad he keeps in his pocket. He has plenty to sort out during the break… Leeds have created the better chances here and Arsenal are looking short of ideas once they get into the opposition half. You can see why Farke’s side are undefeated so far this season.

Justin sweeps up for Leeds when Arsenal try to play head tennis on the Leeds box. Moments before Saka had ended up horizontally in the box when Muharemovic was shielding a long ball back to Trafford. The home crowd wants a penalty but no way.

Ally McCoist is ladling praise on Leeds’ organisation and discipline. And has special garlands for Calvert-Lewin who feels the referee is giving him nothing when manhandled by Konsa and Gabriel.

Three minutes of stoppage time are signalled, almost all for Justin’s splattered nose.

Arsenal were caught offside four times in the opening 16 minutes vs Leeds. That's 24 offsides in Premier League games for the season so far, which is at least twice as many as any every other team (Leeds, Brighton, Spurs 12 each) . https://t.co/jnTQah5bh4

Great save from Raya when Gudmundsson’s thumping volley on the end of Bogle’s superb, deep cross is blocked at the near post. Okafor set the move going with a fine crossfield pass.

Arsenal keep the ball but are being pushed back and forced to horseshoe from right to left wing. Madueke suddenly accelerates and drives towards the box to belt over a cross that havertz, from a very tight angle, heads miles over.

It feels like there’s 15 yellow shirts out there, which is testament to the organisation (and physical size?) of this Leeds team. They have been the better side. Tanaka and Stach are frustrating the Arsenal midfielders.

Two more Leeds names in the book: Ampadu for a late foul on Odegaard and Farke’s when the fourth official dobs him in to referee for something he said.

The crowd is growing frustrated by how well Leeds are playing and how little space they are allowing Arsenal.

Okafor overhits a pass in from the left that would have put Stach through on to the keeper. Then Tanaka is penalised for bodychecking Lewis-Skelly and goes into the book.

Oakfor rolls the ball into an empty net when Raya runs out but the whistle had already gone because Calafiori had triggered the trap perfectly.

Chances at both ends as Raya comes off his line, swats a punch to Amapdu who tries to loop it over him. Raya runs back to catch it and drifts very close to his goal-line. But he then instigates a counter with a brilliant pass out to the left and Madueke crosses fro Saka who is well held off by Muharemovic.

David Raya gets back to his line to keep out the looping header 🧤 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/53ilZvYwAY

It’s been a slow burner but the game is heating up now. That Leeds chance at the back post (Bogle accidentally blocking Stach’s volley) has sent a jolt of nervous electricity around the Emirates. Leeds are looking good at the back and increasingly dangerous in attack.

Ampadu wants to know why Saka isn’t being booked as he fouls Justin, a second foul in 30 seconds by the winger.

Justin is not allowed back on for far too long but eventually gets the nod as Tanaka refuses to be mesmerised by Saka’s footwork, watches the ball, nicks it off him and is tripped by the England winger when he tries to bomb off upfield after his tackle.

Justin affects the Blackadder ‘wibble’ look minus the Y-fronts on his head to continue. A bung up each nostril.

Trafford’s long free-kick is headed back to Raya.

Raya is fouled at the corner. Madueke whacks Justin across the ankles in an undetected foul and the Leeds defender faceplants into the turf and sits up with blood streaming out of his nose.

Another half chance for Leeds when Bogle pops up in the inside-left channel when a cross bypasses Calvert-Lewin. He tries to hook it over Konsa and blast it past Raya who spreads himself to turn it behind.

Good cross from Gudmundsson on the left dips perfectly for Stach to volley but Bogle can’t get out of the way. He is a prolific underlapper and pays the price here, blocking his team-mate’s shot.

Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

It’s the incisive, between-the-lines passes that Arsenal are currently lacking. Perhaps a bit of rustiness after such a long break between games?

Calafiori drives past Bogle and whips over a cross that is behind Havertz who has to backpedal to head it which robs his effort of power. Trafford drops to his knees to gather.

Rice takes an unnecessary touch instead of playing a first-time through ball to Madueke and Leeds recover to attack up the left. Okafor’s cross sails way too long and Bogle cannot keep it in.

Lewis-Skelly holds off Stach but then throws up his arms as if flapping a cape and clocks Stach in the face. Leeds are awarded a free-kick.

Excellent hold-up play by Calvert-Lewin is ruined by a shoddy Amapadu pass. Arsenal move it out to the right where Leeds enmesh White in the offside trap again. The crowd howls in frustration.

Someone seems to be banging a drum. Is this Selhurst Park? Okafor is penalised for grabbing Konsa’s shirt as he tried to spin the centre-back on halfway. Arsenal switch it to their left and Calafiori crashes into the box to cross. The ball deflects through the area and over the penalty spot but there’s no runner to meet it.

As TNT Sports points out, Leeds are trying to press Arsenal high but the positioning of Rice and Lewis-Skelly is much better than it was at Brighton.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal have been eager to play quick passes over the Leeds defence in these opening exchanges. Arteta’s side usually prefer to build up more slowly but they are looking for Havertz quite early. A consequence, perhaps, of Leeds pushing quite high up the pitch.

Okafor’s blistering 20-yard shot is deflected behind for a corner. The linesman’s flag was up because he said Calvert-Lewin had moved towards the ball in an offside position but the referee overrules him.

Arsenal defend the cross solidly but Bogle is covering diligently when they try to play Madueke clear with a long ball.

Now Madueke is caught offside on the left after a Muharemovic mistake threatened to let Havertz burst through before he laid it off instead.

Justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Aresnal launch a counter up the right and the telepathy between White and Saka for once breaks down when White runs offside for a return pass. Elvedi was there to sweep up in any case.

Muharemovic reads the game well and snuffs out a long pass looking for Havertz, shifts the ball up to Calvert-Lewin who is grabbed round the waist by Gabriel and Leeds are awarded a free-kick in the centre-circle.

Saka, miles offside, takes on a cross that he should have headed with a leaping volley instead and Trafford saves at very close range. Slick work between Odegaard and Madueke to get the ball to Saka.

Both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Leeds kick off, attacking from right to left, going all the way back to Trafford standing outside his box and he clips a long pass up the right and Leeds are immediately penalised with the linesman’s flag.

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea says it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1418. Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated ‘pseudobulk’ counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have revealed hundreds of thousands of association signals between genetic variants and human diseases and traits4, but the modes of action by which most of these variants affect phenotypes remain to be characterized, especially non-coding variants. The characterization of the impact of genetic variants on gene expression—known as expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) mapping—can help linking variants to the putative genes they regulate1,5,6,7,8,9, thus identifying the genes and pathways involved in disease pathogenesis, which is a critical step in identifying opportunities for therapeutic intervention10.

However, important limitations remain. First, eQTL mapping has traditionally been limited to common genetic variation (minor allele frequency (MAF)) greater than 1–5%) due to relatively small sample sizes and the widespread use of genotyping arrays, which do not accurately genotype most rare variants and complex structural variants11, compared with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) approaches. Second, eQTLs are extremely context specific, with many studies demonstrating that genetic variants frequently affect gene expression levels in ways detectable only in specific tissues3, sorted cell types6,10,12,13 or on stimulation14,15. Single-cell eQTL mapping has further demonstrated that the effects of many genetic variants on gene expression can only be detected within specific cell types and even transient cellular states3,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,23.

Here we introduce phase 1 of the TenK10K (up to 10,000 cells for 10,000 individuals) study, encompassing 5.4 million cells from 1,925 individuals of European ancestry selected from a broader cohort of 2,103 individuals. In accompanying papers, we leverage the same dataset to investigate the effect of tandem repeat variation on gene expression24 and the putative causal links between gene expression measurements and human diseases and traits25, and an overlapping set of samples to explore the impact of genetic variation on chromatin accessibility26.

Here we use an association method we recently developed, SAIGE-QTL27, to map common-variant and rare-variant single-cell eQTLs across immune cell types. We identify more than 150,000 common-variant effects and more than 30,000 rare-variant effects on gene expression, including signals for nearly 5,000 genes (roughly 25%) with no previously reported eQTLs in a large blood eQTL study5. We propose a framework for quantifying the extent of cell-type specificity or sharedness of eQTLs and show that about half of the effects are found in only one or a few cell types, and almost none are ubiquitous across all. We perform statistical colocalization between our eQTLs and 60 disease phenotypes and blood traits, identifying more than 60,000 colocalization events for more than 5,000 genes, providing potential molecular mechanisms in almost 900 genes associated with human phenotypic variation. We use a biologically driven deep learning method, scDeepID, to identify continuous cell states related to cell function and map more than 15,000 eQTLs that vary dynamically along those states. Finally, we identify 164 independent genetic variants that regulate the abundance of cell states.

After quality control, a total of 5,438,679 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 1,925 donors were considered for analysis (Fig. 1, Supplementary Table 1 and Methods). We collected and sequenced PBMCs from all individuals, yielding an average of 2,825 cells per individual after quality control (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2 and Methods).

a, Overview of the data used in this paper introducing phase 1 of the TenK10K cohort. High-quality matched WGS and scRNA-seq data were generated for 1,925 individuals of European ancestry (after quality control). After computational analysis and processing, we conducted both common and rare-variant eQTL analysis and identified cell-type-specific and state-specific effects of genetic regulation in immune cells. We also performed colocalization analysis with GWAS from 60 traits and diseases and mapped QTLs affecting csaQTL. b, Accompanying papers perform complementary analyses using the TenK10K phase 1 cohort. In brief, ref. 25 integrates sc-eQTLs from the present study and 100 GWAS studies to explain the causal role of gene expression in immune cell types across complex traits; ref. 24 uses the WGS data to generate a catalogue of more than 1.7 million polymorphic tandem repeats and dissect their effects on single-cell-resolved gene expression; ref. 26 combines common genetic variants called from WGS with scATAC-seq generated for a subset of roughly 1,000 individuals to investigate the genetic regulation of chromatin accessibility at cellular resolution. c, Schematic of the 28 immune cell types identified, organized by main cell type. d, The number of cells available for analysis by cell type for the 28 immune cell types is summarized in d. Top, bar plot showing total cell numbers per cell type on a log10 scale; bottom, violin plots showing the distribution across individuals on a log10 scale. ASDC, AXL+SIGLEC6+ dendritic cells; cDC1/2, conventional type 1/2 dendritic cells; CD4CTL, CD4+ cytotoxic T cells; dnT,  double-negative T cells; gdT, γδ T cells; ILC, innate lymphoid cells; MAIT, mucosal-associated invariant T cells; pDC, plasmacytoid dendritic cells. Panels created in BioRender: a, Cuomo, A. https://biorender.com/0bkvg8x (2026); c, Cuomo, A. https://biorender.com/fyk570b (2026).

Each cell was assigned to their donor of origin by means of demultiplexing and to an immune cell type using a combined approach of reference-based classification and hierarchical clustering as recommended by the single-cell eQTLGen Consortium28 (Methods). Each cell was assigned to one of 28 different cell types, spanning the key expected immune lineages (Fig. 1c, Supplementary Fig. 3 and Supplementary Table 2).

In addition, we generated WGS data for all 1,925 individuals, which was processed and quality-controlled using established pipelines (Methods). We called 66,658,242 sites across single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and insertions and deletions (indels), of which 53,784,018 (80.6%) were rare (MAF < 1%), roughly 4.5 times as many as from SNP array data (Methods and Supplementary Fig. 4).

To assess the effects of common genetic variation on gene expression changes, we mapped cis eQTLs, testing for the effects of common (MAF > 1%) variant sites within ±100 kilobases (kb) of the gene body on single-cell expression profiles (testing all sufficiently expressed genes; Methods). We used SAIGE-QTL27 to map eQTL effects using single-cell profiles modelled as Poisson counts, rather than relying on ‘pseudobulk’ aggregation. We mapped eQTLs separately in each of the 28 cell types and confirmed the type I error was controlled using permutations (Fig. 2a). At a false discovery rate (FDR) of less than 5%, we identified 154,932 eQTLs in at least one cell type from 17,674 unique eGenes (83% of all genes tested; Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 5). The number of eQTLs identified varied substantially across cell types, largely due to the number of cells available for each cell type and the resulting number of individuals tested affecting statistical power, as previously shown in refs. 16,27 (Fig. 2b, Extended Data Fig. 1 and Supplementary Table 2).

a, Quantile–quantile plot for all common (MAF = 1%, top) and rare (MAF < 1%, bottom) variant eQTL results across 28 immune cell types. For the most abundant cell type, CD4TCM cells, we shuffled individual IDs and reperformed the test to assess calibration (labelled ‘permuted control’). Colour represents cell type, as shown in the legend in the top right. The observed P values are those from the main analysis using SAIGE-QTL (Methods). b, Number of eGenes identified (solid colour) compared to the total number of genes tested (faded) across cell types. Top, common-variant eQTL mapping (single-variant tests); bottom, rare-variant eGenes using combined P values of burden and SKAT tests. The middle bar plots represent the number of cells and individuals available for each cell type to demonstrate their role in the power differences across cell types. For representative cell types, the percentage of eGenes compared to the total number of genes tested is highlighted. Percentages for all cell types are available at Supplementary Table 2. c,d, For all genes with more than one independent signal identified confidently by fine mapping (posterior inclusion probability (PIP) > 0.9, using SuSiE2; Methods) signals (credible sets) were categorized as either primary (including the top most significant variant) or non-primary. Non-primary signals are on average found further away from the gene’s TSS, less likely to be found in promoter regions (c) and more likely in enhancer regions compared with primary signals (d). In c, violin plots represent distribution over n = 17,674 independent signals, and the horizontal lines in the box plots therein represent the first quartile, median and third quartile. e, Proportion of eQTLs identified in each cell type by means of fine mapping, coloured by the number of independent signals (‘only one’ or ‘two or more’).

We performed fine mapping using SuSiE29 (Methods), showing an extra 24,925 (a 16% increase) non-primary (secondary, tertiary and so on)30,31 eQTL signals for 7,131 eGenes (40.4%). We used 95% credible sets to quantify the number of independent signals for each eGene, and explored differences between primary effects (variants from the credible set containing the top variant for each eGene) and non-primary effects (all other credible sets). We find that primary effects contain larger credible sets, and genes in the higher-proportion cell types have substantially more non-primary effects (Fig. 2e and Supplementary Fig. 6). As shown by others31, non-primary signals were found further from the transcription start site (TSS) and more likely in enhancer as opposed to promoter regions (Fig. 2c,d).

We compared the eGenes we identified with those from bulk blood eQTL studies. First, we considered the eQTLGen consortium study5: the largest eQTL study so far in whole blood. We identified a comparable number of eGenes compared to eQTLGen (17,674 and 16,987, respectively), despite the 15-fold smaller sample size (1,925 compared with more than 30,000 individuals; Extended Data Fig. 2a). More than one-quarter of our eGenes were not identified in eQTLGen (n = 4,572, 25.9%); those genes were slightly more lowly expressed, and their expression was more cell-type-specific (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c) compared with eGenes found by both studies; TenK10K-unique eGenes were also more likely to be eGenes in fewer cell types overall, in rare cell types (n < 60,000) compared with more abundant ones or in one cell type only (‘cell-type-specific’, Extended Data Fig. 2d–f), demonstrating the importance of mapping eQTLs at cellular resolution. Conversely, 23% of eQTLGen eGenes were not detected in our study: these were extremely lowly expressed across all 28 cell types (average expression 4% as opposed to roughly 30% for shared eGenes; Extended Data Fig. 2b).

An alternative approach to detect cell-type-specific eQTLs is bulk eQTL mapping on sorted cell types, which has proved to be well-powered even with modest sample sizes. We compared our eQTLs to four such studies (BLUEPRINT6 and CEDAR13, and refs. 10 and 12), matching cell types like for like. Overall, we demonstrate similar to much-increased power to identify cell-type-specific eQTLs, although we note the much larger sample size used in this study. Our study provides assessment of more granular cell types (n = 28) than many previous studies using sorted immune cell types (for example, 13 in ref. 10; Extended Data Fig. 3).

Compared with the OneK1K study16, the previously largest single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTL) map in blood, we identified nearly three times as many eGenes (17,674 compared with 6,469). This reflects several factors, including the increased power from both larger sample size (about twice the individuals: 1,925 compared with 982), number of cells per individual (2,825 compared with 1,291), the consequent more granular cell-type resolution (28 compared with 14 cell types) and the increased power due to modelling single-cell expression profiles rather than pseudobulk. The eGenes identified in our study, rather than OneK1K, were less highly expressed and more likely to be expressed in fewer cell types (in our data; Supplementary Fig. 7).

Finally, to quantify the improvement from cell-type resolution within our data, we compared the eQTLs identified separately in each cell type with a new set of eQTLs obtained from pseudobulk expression values aggregated across all 28 cell types (Methods). At FDR < 5%, this pseudobulk analysis identified 11,359 eGenes, similar to the number found in our most abundant cell type, the CD4+ central memory T (CD4TCM) cells, and nearly 30% fewer than when we consider all eGenes identified in at least one cell type (Extended Data Fig. 4).

We correlated our eQTL effect sizes with promoter-activity scores from PromoterAI32 for each gene’s lead variant across cell types, finding good agreement (median correlation 0.66; Supplementary Fig. 8 and Methods).

Most eQTL studies so far8,9,16,17 have focused on common genetic variants (MAF ≥ 1–5%). Studies investigating the effects of rare variants (MAF < 1%) on tissue-level gene expression7,33 have conducted ‘outlier analyses’, in which rare variants are sought specifically in individuals with extreme expression levels for a given gene rather than performing systematic population-level assessments.

Using SNPs and indels from WGS and SAIGE-QTL, we mapped the effects of rare variation (MAF < 1%) within a cis window (±100 kb) around each gene’s body, using gene-set-based tests for increased power (Methods). For each cell type, we tested for the effects of local rare variants on all sufficiently expressed genes (Methods) using two tests designed to capture different regulatory mechanisms: the burden test, and the sequence kernel association test (SKAT)34.

Overall, we observe 34,376 rare-variant signals across all cell types for 10,005 unique rare eGenes (47% of all genes tested) after FDR correction on the combined P values from the burden and SKAT tests (FDR < 5%; Fig. 2b, Supplementary Fig. 9 and Methods). Type I error was well-controlled for the rare-variant tests (Fig. 2a), and the number of cells per cell type was highly correlated with the number of eGenes identified (correlation 0.98, Extended Data Fig. 1).

Most eGenes were identified by SKAT alone (29,260, 85%), followed by both SKAT and burden (4,975, 14.5%) and burden alone (141, 0.5%). This is consistent with SKAT being more appropriate when variants in the set have mixed direction of effects (that is, some increasing, some decreasing gene expression), which we expect in a regulatory context (Fig. 3a).

a, Bar plot showing the proportion of rare eGenes identified using the different set-based tests—identified as eGenes at FDR < 5% by the burden test, the SKAT test or both—across cell types. b, Number of eGenes identified at P < 10−6 identified when testing for association using only functionally annotated (solid colour) or all-cis (faded colour) rare variants (Methods), using SKAT. Each plot represents a different cell type (n = 26). c, Locus zoom plot of rare genetic variants associated with the SH2D2A gene on chromosome 1 in CD4TCM cells, with the leading genetic variants annotated. LD variants are variants in perfect LD with the annotated putatively causal ones. Bottom plot, zoom in on the chromatin accessibility profile across representative cell types for each main group around the SH2D2A gene and with the top variant (1:156816831:A:AC) shown as a vertical line. The P values shown are from the single-variant tests for rare variants using SAIGE-QTL (Methods). d, Locus zoom plot of rare genetic variants associated with the TMED3 gene on chromosome 15 in NK cells, with the leading splice-altering genetic variant (15:79311418:G:A) annotated. Bottom plot shows AlphaGenome-predicted RNA-seq coverage, splice sites usage and splice sites tracks for exon 1 and 2 of the TMED3 gene for the 15:79311418:G:A variant (ALT, yellow) and reference (REF, green) alleles.
