#1308. The Dominik Szoboszlai dilemma: One of Europe's best midfielders who Liverpool must build around? Or a square peg who they play better without? This is what Andoni Iraola should do

Published: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EDT, 3 November 2026

The folks in Liverpool’s commercial team devoted a fair portion of last season chasing after Dominik Szoboszlai.

As the club's player of the month more often than not, the Hungarian was obliged to fulfil a swathe of sponsorship duties and, like for many defenders last season, tying down Szoboszlai was not always easy. But he always completed these extracurricular activities, and was rewarded with a bumper new contract.

The midfielder was the standard-setter in pre-season and made vice-captain, with an eye on becoming the next man to wear the armband permanently when Virgil van Dijk eventually leaves. Szoboszlai’s role as protagonist continued in Andoni Iraola’s first competitive match with a last-gasp thunderous strike at Newcastle. Everything at Liverpool, it seemed, revolved around this handsome, chiseled star with a swagger.

Fast forward two months, however, and that's no longer the case. Szoboszlai has gone from first name on the teamsheet to having to fight for a starting spot. For some fans, he has become the scapegoat.

That seems wholly unfair but they point to the fact his half an hour from the bench against Arsenal coincided with Liverpool ceding control, balance and threat. Before that, Szoboszlai had missed four-and-a-half games – he went off injured early in a win at Brentford – and the Reds won all of them.

So, are Liverpool really better without the Hungarian? Let’s analyse both sides of the argument.

Would Andoni Iraola (right) really be better off without Dominik Szoboszlai (right)?

FOR: Drop him, he doesn’t fit Iraola’s system

The case against Szoboszlai revolves around balance, control and space.

Is it a coincidence that Florian Wirtz’s best run in a Liverpool shirt came in the last month, when the German had two midfielders behind him who were happy to do the defensive dirty work?

With both Szoboszlai and Wirtz in the side, it feels like the pair get in each other’s way and try to occupy the same positions, and Liverpool in turn are vulnerable to the counter-attack.

Alexis Mac Allister is enjoying his best form in well over a year and likes to arrive late into the box, but he cannot do this with Szoboszlai next to him as it leaves his team too exposed going the other way.

Young Trey Nyoni is a classy midfielder who thrives at dropping deep to start attacks and bait opposition presses. The 19-year-old is happy to sit back and allow those in front of him to thrive, such as Mac Allister playing a box-to-box role.

When Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled.

When Trey Nyoni went off for Szoboszlai against Arsenal, Iraola’s side lost this balance and their chances of getting back into the game dwindled

Szoboszlai is arrogant but has every right to be.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. A goal threat with one of the fiercest long shots in the game, with dead-ball precision, he is every bit the player Liverpool thought they were buying from RB Leipzig in 2023.

The midfielder has an engine akin to Declan Rice and is tireless in his work rate.

Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him. As shown last term, he can win matches on his own. Despite his recent lay-off, he is barely injured and is a standard-bearer on the training pitch.

Iraola’s system is a 4-2-3-1 on paper but the Basque wants a bit of everything from his midfield: one No6, one No8 and one No10. Szoboszlai can play each of those roles. He has a tattoo of a Steven Gerrard quote and is the closest player to the former skipper that Anfield has seen since.

Internally, Liverpool believe Szoboszlai’s best years are ahead of him. In signing him up to a five-year deal at the end of last season – a process led by former sporting director Richard Hughes with the player’s agent Matyas Esterhazy – the Reds hierarchy were glad to stave off any future approaches from the likes of Real Madrid.

On his day, he is one of the best midfielders in Europe. Surely, any team would want him and he is so talented that managers should build around him

There are four solutions, two of which are outlined above: drop him and have a more balanced midfield or play him and benefit from his goal-scoring and creative powers, plus leadership and relentless running.

Another option may not be popular but there is a Wirtz-shaped elephant in the room. Does Iraola bench Wirtz and play Szoboszlai as the No10?

He’d have fewer defensive duties so the control and balance remains, but the Hungarian would pop up in dangerous areas to cause issues. Wirtz is a creative wizard when on form but how many times does he pass up an opportunity to shoot? Szoboszlai would already be wheeling away in celebration by the time Wirtz has made his mind up on what to do with an attack.

And then there is the compromise of Szoboszlai at right back. The player himself does not like it as he feels less important in that position, but it solves a lot of issues including all the aforementioned balance and control quirks. It also adds one thing that is bothering Iraola – creativity and attacking verve from right back.

The downside of this is Liverpool would lose the defensive acumen and physicality of aerial presence of Ronald Araujo, who is currently enjoying cult hero status at right back.

Szoboszlai is a strong right back but does not like playing there as he believes he has less influence on the game

The best teams build around the best players. There are always similar debates around Erling Haaland at Manchester City and anyone who argues the case to drop him is made to look silly.

So I will say the same about Szoboszlai. It is on Iraola to make it work. Most managers would kill for a depth of midfield talent like he has. Why not play him at right back? It solves multiple issues at once and Liverpool can finally replace the creativity Trent Alexander-Arnold used to bring from that role.

If Liverpool are seeing a game out, they can push Szoboszlai to the No 10, sub off Wirtz and bring on a true defender to help the physical battle.

Liverpool will be reunited with an old friend on Wednesday – and former cult hero Dirk Kuyt is relishing the chance to beat his old team.

Kuyt, played 285 times for the Reds between 2006 and 2012, scoring 71 times – and will face his old team for the first time on Wednesday as manager of Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The Dutchman took over last week after a spell as assistant manager and said: ‘As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how much Fenerbahce and Liverpool mean to me.

‘It will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we're in, I'm not here for myself. I'm here for the club and that's what is important – to show the fans who deserve much more.

‘If we show up tomorrow with good energy, with passion and there to play, it can be a very special night.

‘Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce. If the fans show up, I think Europe will see how big this fan base is.’

Liverpool have happy memories in Istanbul having won this competition here in 2005 – though they lost twice to Galatasaray in Turkey last season, in the league phase and then last-16.

Fenerbahce play on the Asian side of the city and have familiar faces such as Romelu Lukaku, N'Golo Kante, Ederson, Nathan Ake and Mason Greenwood.

Liverpool will be without midfielder Ryan Gravenberch, who has a heel problem.

Boss Andoni Iraola said he liked a lot of the performance against Arsenal on Sunday but his side still need to improve.

‘It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day,’ he said. ‘I liked a lot of things but we still need to improve, especially attacking the box.'

#1307. Fabregas: ‘Como will face wild atmosphere in Lens, quality of Thauvin’

Cesc Fabregas warns Como that there will be a ‘wild atmosphere’ against RC Lens in the Champions League tomorrow and he is keeping a close eye on Florian Thauvin.

It kicks off at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis in Lens on Wednesday at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

The Lariani are in their first ever Champions League campaign and doing remarkably well, winning both home matches with four goals scored against RB Leipzig and Manchester United, but losing away to Feyenoord.

While RC Lens might not seem to be on paper as big as those sides, Fabregas warns they are not to be underestimated on home turf.

“It’s a wild atmosphere, I played here two or three times for Monaco, I love nights like this, because you can feel the passion even during the warm-up,” Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia.

“It will be interesting and a marvellous experience for our players. We wanted these nights, so if you are not motivated to play these, then you’re in the wrong job.”

There is a familiar face to Italian football, as former Udinese man Florian Thauvin has flourished since his return to France.

“Thauvin is an incredible player, he was at Marseille, then we faced him for Udinese. He makes the difference, has huge quality, scores a lot of goals, so he is the reference point for this team, and we need to keep a close eye on him.”

Como are perhaps no longer a surprise outfit at this stage, so what will their ambitions be if they win here tomorrow?

“We will try to win and then see what happens, but this season is a whole new experience for Como, our world is opening up. If we get a good result, then we’ll see how to go into the final four games, but we have to keep taking it one game at a time,” added Fabregas.

“There’s no point thinking about what might happen, we just need to enjoy these nights.”

While Como would in the past need to score lots of goals to win fixtures, they seem to have found different ways of approaching tests now.

“We need to be able to handle different situations. We played 39 games the first season, 43 the second, this year it’ll be at least 47-48, it might be over 50, so that means we need to balance out the energy.

“There are moments where we need to control the situation, because I remember last season we were great for the first 60 minutes and then fell away at the end. We cannot do that this term, so we’re more alert about that.”

Como also have a huge game coming up in Serie A against Inter this weekend, but they have limited players available, with Trevoh Chalobah, Moise Kean, Jesus Rodriguez, Assane Diao and Jayden Addai out of action.

“Chalobah isn’t ready for this game, we’ll see on Sunday. We are a little penalised in the Champions League because of the list, so we’ve got only 15 players tomorrow. That makes preserving energy tougher in this tournament, but Serie A remains the most important competition.”

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died as a result of a freak accident during the Spanish second division match against FC Andorra, so Fabregas wanted to send a message.

“In such a wonderful sport as football, it is honestly hard to deal with things like this. I send my heart to his father and mother, I am a parent, and the idea of going to see your son playing in a match and life can end in a moment, it makes you think.

“It was a huge blow, I cannot imagine the pain they are feeling, so I send an embrace to his family, to his teammates who experienced that, it can never be forgotten.”

#1305. How Many Games Jesus Owono Could Be Banned For After Colliding with Jesus de Miguel

How many games Jesus Owono could be set to miss after colliding with Jesus de Miguel has now emerged, following the striker's tragic passing early on Tuesday morning.

CD Tenerife had initially provided a worrying update on their player's neurological condition at 4am local time, confirming that De Miguel had suffered a cardiac arrest after taking a high knee from the opposition goalkeeper.

Four hours later, it was announced that he had passed away in hospital, having been rushed there after his side's Spanish second-tier clash against FC Andorra, which was poised at 2-2, had been abandoned following the distressing scenes.

An update has since emerged on Owono, with the goalkeeper reportedly seen 'crying and praying' in the dressing room after the shocking incident. And now, with Spanish police having launched an investigation, the potential punishment he could face has been outlined.

According to Guillem Balague, a renowned Spanish journalist, the RFEF has suspended today's Cup matchday, some of which had already been moved a week because of the Urda train accident.

Tenerife have asked to postpone Saturday's League game against Granada and Tuesday's Cup tie against Badajoz, and the League and RFEF are expected to accept that request. Ballague also wrote (See his full post below):

"[Jesus] Owono faces a ban of four to eight matches, or even more for the extreme consequence of his clash with de Miguel."

.Any current footballing investigations will likely look towards the intent of the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international, though any legal action is currently considered unlikely.

As per the same report, it is unlikely that Owono will face criminal charges that many on social media - mainly through online abuse directed at the goalkeeper - have called for.

Police have launched an investigation because there has been a death, and that always happens as standard protocol, but it is almost impossible that anything comes of it.

As per Ballague, the tackle was a circumstance of the game, and Spanish Supreme Court doctrine (STS 379/2025) only brings in criminal law where there was clear intent to hurt, and it isn't related to the game.

#1304. Prince William and Prince George cut frustrated figures in the directors' box as they watch their beloved Aston Villa lose 3-0 to Barcelona on rain-soaked night in Spain

Published: 15:19 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 23:02 EDT, 3 November 2026

Prince William was in the stands to watch Aston Villa in Champions League action, with the Prince of Wales taking in his side's clash with Barcelona from the directors' box.

The 44-year-old has been a fan of the club since his days at Eton, when he shunned the more conventional Premier League big beasts supported by his schoolmates.

Since then, the Prince has followed Villa over land and sea and he was in position at the newly-renovated Camp Nou where he saw things get off to the worst possible start for his side when Lamine Yamal capitalised on a defensive howler to make it 1-0 to the hosts in the seventh minute.

It got worse for them in the second half, with a double from former Leeds United star Raphinha ensuring a 3-0 defeat.

Earlier, Barcelona posted a welcome on X, which read: 'FC Barcelona is honoured to welcome His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales and His Royal Highness Prince George to the Spotify Camp Nou. Thank you for joining us for a special evening of Champions League football featuring your beloved Aston Villa.'

Prince William is no stranger to European travel, last week travelling to Istanbul to watch Villa thump six past Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The result at the Nou Camp ended Villa's perfect start in the league phase of the Champions League, with Emery's side having won their opening two fixtures.

Prince William with Prince George after Aston Villa concede early on against Barcelona

The royals watched Lamine Yamal open the scoring for Barcelona early on

Rain poured down at the Nou Camp as they watched Villa lose 3-0 against the Spanish giants

Istanbul will have happy memories for Prince William and his team after he followed them to the final of last season's Europa League, which took place at Besiktas Stadium.

Previously, the Prince has travelled to destinations abroad including Paris to watch his beloved side, as well as regularly watching matches at home at Villa Park.

When asked about why he settled on the Midlands club, Prince William shared that it was the thrill of supporting a club without season after season of successes which had brought him to Aston Villa.

'A long time ago at school I got into football big time. I was looking around for clubs. All my friends were either Man United fans or Chelsea fans and I didn’t want to follow the run-of-the-mill teams,' he told the BBC in 2015.

'I wanted to have a team that was more mid-table that could give me more emotional rollercoaster moments.

FC Barcelona is honoured to welcome His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales and His Royal Highness Prince George to the Spotify Camp Nou.Thank you for joining us for a special evening of Champions League football featuring your beloved Aston Villa. pic.twitter.com/pCZg7PI8On

'Aston Villa’s always had a great history. I have got friends of mine who support Aston Villa and one of the first FA Cup games I went to was Bolton v Aston Villa back in 2000. Sadly, Villa went on to lose to Chelsea (in the final),' he said

'It was fantastic, I sat with all the fans with my red beanie on, and I was with all the Brummie fans and had a great time.

'It was the atmosphere, the camaraderie and I really felt that there was something I could connect with.'

#1303. Is research funding now a lottery? Elite funder ERC swamped by applications

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

When grant programmes’ success rates are pushed down below a certain threshold, they essentially become a lottery.Credit: javier rodriguez jimenez/Shutterstock

A 60% growth in applications to one of the world’s most prestigious research-grant programmes could result in an exceptionally low success rate, raising fears that quality scientific ideas will go unfunded. This rise is attributable, in part, to the ease of writing applications with artificial-intelligence tools.

When the best decision is no decision: the rise of randomization in grant funding

When the best decision is no decision: the rise of randomization in grant funding

“The number is a bit scary,” says Maria Leptin, president of the European Research Council (ERC) in Brussels, noting that it’s increasingly difficult for their staff and peer reviewers to tackle so many applications.

The ERC’s Starting Grant programme — which offers base funds of up to €1.5 million (US$1.7 million) over five years to early-career scientists — received 7,710 proposals for 2027 grants before the deadline on 14 October, up from 4,807 last year (see ‘Rising torrent’).

With up to 373 grants available, down from 421 last year because of funding constraints, that will mean a success rate of less than 5%, compared with 8.8% for the 2026 grant call. “It’s almost a lottery,” says Devang Mehta, a systems and synthetic biologist at the Catholic University of Leuven in Belgium who applied for a Starting Grant this year.

The ERC is the Europe Union’s elite funder of basic research, and has an annual budget of nearly €3 billion. It offers three grant categories — Starting, Consolidator and Advanced — for individual researchers at growing stages of seniority. All have seen significant increases in applications in recent years.

Europe as science superpower: what it will take to rival the US and China

Europe as science superpower: what it will take to rival the US and China

Similar rises in research-grant applications are happening worldwide, says Lynn Kamerlin, a molecular biologist at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta who has studied grant success rates1. An ideal success rate for grant programmes is about 20%, she says. Any lower and it becomes increasingly difficult to select the best research without subjective judging, meaning that a lot of good science will go unfunded, she adds. “People can’t tell the difference between the top 6, 8, 12%.”

She suggests that one solution is to have a panel select the top 20% of applications and then pick winners at random, as some funders are doing. Anything below that threshold “is a lottery anyhow”, she says.

The rise in submissions has been attributed in part to artificial intelligence making it simpler to write grant applications. “It’s just so much easier to generate text,” says Kamerlin. That’s putting huge pressure on the system, she says, because “it can spin absolute nonsense”, meaning that reviews of applications require greater scrutiny.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03476-3

Correction 28 October 2026: The original version of this article noted a 62% growth in applications to the European Research Council’s Starting Grant programme from 2026 to 2027. In fact, the rise was 60%.

Kamerlin, S. C. L. EMBO Rep 27, 2145–2146 (2026).

#1302. Keith Hackett Claims Liverpool vs Arsenal Ref Should Be ‘Suspended’

Howard Webb has been urged to keep Andy Madley away from Premier League fixtures this weekend after his performance during Liverpool vs Arsenal drew criticism.

Several incidents occurred as Mikel Arteta's side won at Anfield for the first time in 14 years. Both teams felt decisions could've gone for them, with each situation receiving huge attention in the aftermath.

Young midfielder Trey Nyoni went unpunished for a strong early challenge, Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt inside the box, and Alexis Mac Allister went to ground after going head-to-head with Noni Madueke.

Fans on social media have continued to debate whether spot kicks or red cards should've been awarded. Now, former head of the PGMOL Keith Hackett has given his thoughts.

Hackett, speaking to Football Insider, admitted he was surprised to see Madley given the biggest fixture of the weekend in the first place. He said: "I was surprised, having watched his recent performances, that Andy Madley was appointed to this game.

Szoboszlai's comments have gone down well with Arsenal supporters.

"We have elite referees within the group. We have a pecking order, and those referees that are in form should get this game."

He went a step further and suggested that if he were in Howard Webb's shoes, Madley would be stood down for the upcoming gameweek. Hackett continued:

"There are going to be knocks on the door saying, 'Boss, why haven't I got a game?' And I would be saying, 'You need to improve your performance and be more consistent.'

"I don't think he had his best game, and I don't know what his best game is. We've highlighted a number of ifs, and I've highlighted one that is 100 per cent incorrect.

"That says to me, next week if I was doing the appointments, he ain't got a game."

Speaking during the match, the former FIFA referee claimed the home team would feel 'aggrieved' at Madley and VAR's decision not to award a penalty for Timber's pull on Isak.

"Liverpool will feel really aggrieved at half-time. Replays showing, very clearly, that Arsenal's Timber had a fistful of the shirt of Isak. As Isak jumps to head the ball, he was prevented from making contact - that is a clear penalty kick," he said.

"We ask once again: Where was the referee positioned? Why didn't he take action? If he was poorly positioned and didn't see the offence, then this surely is what VAR is for. VAR should have intervened, the pull impacted on the forward heading the ball. It was a clear penalty kick."

"VAR: 'All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal.'"

So Madley missed the penalty and everyone is talking about it but he also missed two incidents of Nyoni raking the achillies of two Arsenal players in the first 10 minutes. By allowing these two incidents to be unpunished he set a precedence for the type of fouls that he was about to allow.

If you look at the Mateta sending off the day before it is hard to recognise the difference. If the media were to concentrate their minds on the many differences in various refereeing decisions instead of trying to whip up a storm over the one progress about erratic refereeing might be made.

#1301. Roma ‘have faith in Vasquez’ against Manchester United amid new problems

Roma director Tony D’Amico assures they ‘have faith’ in third choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez against Manchester United and reveals why Gian Piero Gasperini didn’t speak to the media.

It kicks off at Old Trafford at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CEST).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Feyenoord vs. Inter on the Liveblog.

The Giallorossi were shaken by fresh injury problems just hours before the match, as goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini hurt his back in the last training session.

He was given pain-killing injections, but they were not sufficient, so Devis Vasquez had to step in as their third choice, seeing as Mile Svilar has already been out of action for a month.

It was originally meant to be coach Gasperini who held the media duties pre-match, but seeing as Roma were late getting to the stadium due to traffic in Manchester, it was decided that director of sport D’Amico would take over.

“We took longer than expected to get here without a police escort, but we’re here now, these things happen,” D’Amico told Sky Sport Italia.

“Gollini felt back pain this morning, we tried to get him back in shape, but didn’t manage it, we have faith in Vasquez. This is an opportunity for him, he is one of the four goalkeepers at our disposal and these things happen.

“He will have a big chance and we are confident he can have a good game.”

This is only the latest setback for a side that is already missing Paulo Dybala, Manu Koné and Lorenzo Pellegrini too.

Nonetheless, they have lost only one match all season, the 4-3 defeat to Real Madrid in a game they were leading 3-1 going into the 82nd minute.

#1300. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

#1299. Big Mistake: Newcastle Must Replace Jaissle With Nagelsmann ASAP

Newcastle United's poor start to the Premier League season continued on Monday night as the team fell to a 1-0 defeat at home to Everton.

Thierno Barry's second half goal was the difference between the sides, as the Magpies suffered a fourth defeat in nine games so far this season, and slipped down to 13th in the table, just four points above the relegation zone.

The defeat means Newcastle have now lost four of their last five games in all competitions and five of their last seven, and the level of performance has seen many fans and members of the media question whether the decision to appoint Matthias Jaissle as Eddie Howe's replacement was the right one.

When Howe surprisingly resigned just two weeks before the season began, the Saudi owners moved quickly to bring the German into the job because of his attacking style of football.

The season started well, too, with a draw against Liverpool at Anfield and a win over Tottenham, but since then the style of football has looked unsustainable with this squad. Jaissle has struggled to make the team pick up their tasks properly; the new signings are largely struggling to make an immediate impact, and he doesn't seem to trust his entire squad.

After the defeat to Everton, Jaissle publicly switched the blame to his players too, accusing them of going against the game plan by playing long balls despite him wanting the exact opposite.

"There is big frustration & disappointment. We could not not transfer what we saw in the week, training in a high level. Since the start of the game, not much was seen. That is difficult to understand.

"We were not brave enough to break the line and play on the ground. We saw it in training, but there was almost nothing to see from these aspects in the game. In possession, this was not the level we wanted to see.

"If you just play long balls, it’s not the style Osula prefers & that was not the plan. We need to analyse this in depth, why we could not start the game how we planned. I’m responsible for that, to make it work.

"We have a clear identity of how we want to play. To bring the opposition in stressful situations high in the pitch. We spoke about creating 1-on-1 situations. The plan was not to shoot the long balls."

When the management and players begin to go head-to-head, things usually only end in one way, and that is with a change in the dugout.

But Newcastle don't need to wait for results to worsen, or for the situation to get to a point of no return to make a change. They can get ahead of the curve, admit that his appointment was a mistake, and make an ambitious move to replace him with someone who is undoubtedly better.

With Jaissle seemingly on his way out at St James' Park sooner rather than later, barring any big turnarounds, Newcastle should be assessing their options to replace him.

Eddie Howe is obviously not going to return having just left, but Julian Nagelsmann is a manager who is available immediately and could make a huge difference to the squad. He and Jaissle play a similar style of football having both come through the ranks in Germany, but Nagelsmann has got experience at the highest level.

Having been described as a 'genius', he has the authority and coaching ability to come in and make a change quickly, and the current squad is likely to suit him well. He also has plenty of experience working with younger players, which can see him develop the likes of Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Toure, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, and others.

With so many mangerial vacancies reportedly set to open, Newcastle don't want to miss out on someone who would be the perfect candidate for them, and this is a move the owners should be looking closely at doing quickly, or else they may regret it.

Newcastle suffered yet another disappointing defeat on Monday night as they succumbed to a 1-0 loss against Everton at home.

#1298. Marotta: ‘Inter learn from mistakes in Champions League, Icardi not part of plans’

Inter President Beppe Marotta insists they are ‘learning from mistakes’ in the Champions League as they face Feyenoord, and Mauro Icardi is ‘not in our plans, we aren’t looking for a fifth striker.’

It kicks off at the Stadion De Kuip in Rotterdam at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Manchester United vs. Roma on the Liveblog.

This has been a difficult season so far for the Nerazzurri, more so in the Champions League after defeats to Real Madrid and Club Brugge, then scraping a 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk when down to 10 men.

However, they also suffered their first Serie A defeat of the campaign, losing the Derby della Madonnina 3-1 to Milan on Saturday evening.

“Winning the Champions League of course is a target everyone would like to achieve, and this squad didn’t quite get there despite great results like winning the Scudetto, Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana,” noted Marotta on Sky Sport Italia.

“We learned from the mistakes made along the way, so we hope to eventually climb this mountain that is filled with obstacles and hidden dangers.”

Inter dropped three points off Serie A leaders Lazio with their defeat to Milan, but the reigning holders of both the Scudetto and Coppa Italia are still the title favourites.

“The team, coach and club speak on a daily basis, this is a very healthy group because there are no bad apples,” assured Marotta.

“We can win or lose, but I want to point out Inter lost only three of the last 40 Serie A matches, and those were all against Milan.”

There was news today that Inter activated the clause to extend Federico Dimarco’s contract, but that is only for one season, while others like Hakan Calhanoglu are still waiting for talks.

“We are not feeling anxious, there are many clubs in a similar situation,” assured the President.

“The only player whose contract is running down is Calhanoglu, but we have a very good rapport with him. Dimarco is a pure Inter fan, we exercised this option to extend for a year and during the next few months we’ll be able to discuss a further extension, because he confirmed his desire to stay, and we want him to continue too. A sense of belonging is very important.”

Inter have a striker shortage, as a flu bug swept through the squad to take out Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny in the derby, so with Lautaro Martinez injured, it left Marcus Thuram as the only forward.

Marotta was asked about reports free agent Icardi had proposed himself to Inter as a potential new signing, a return to the club where he played from 2013 to 2019.

“I don’t know who he proposed himself to, but we didn’t hear anything about it,” insisted the President.

“This is a player who gave a lot to Inter, but honestly, he is not part of our plans, just as we are not looking for a fifth striker. It was a fluke that the absences were all in the same area of the team, but we have no problem with goals, as we are one of the most prolific sides in Italy.

“Cristian Chivu is a modern coach who knows how to get the best out of players.”

#1297. 'Divisive' teacher's pet who players roll their eyes at? Or obsessive who truly cares? Man United insiders reveal what Bruno Fernandes' team-mates really think of him - as we reveal Michael Carrick decided to drop captain BEFORE his Como rant

Published: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 30 October 2026

The expression on the faces of Manchester United’s players turned to shock and shame as they left the pitch at Old Trafford on Sunday and ran the gauntlet of fan anger.

No sooner had head coach Michael Carrick been cheered down the tunnel after a 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth left him on the brink of the sack than supporters rounded on the team and a torrent of abuse rained down from the Stretford End.

‘It was a wake-up for all the players,’ one source told Daily Mail Sport this week.

For captain Bruno Fernandes, it was a particularly painful moment. Fernandes was still in his tracksuit bottoms and hoodie having been dropped to the bench and left there to stew by Carrick as United’s season hit a new low.

He is used to the adoration of fans, but their reaction was muted to say the least when he left the dugout to warm up in the second half.

It was the culmination of the hardest two weeks of Fernandes’ seven-year career at United.

Bruno Fernandes has had the hardest two weeks of his Man United career. The lowest point came when he was hooked off in a 4-1 defeat in Como - then took aim at Michael Carrick in his post-match interview

Fernandes was left on the bench for United's loss to Bournemouth, and didn't receive the adulation he's used to getting from the home supporters at Old Trafford

The 32-year-old was struggling for form and fitness this season long before Carrick replaced him in the 67th minute of the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.

Afterwards, he was accused of throwing his head coach under the bus by publicly blaming the tactics and lack of bravery for United’s worst European defeat in 32 years.

Fernandes was unaware at the time that his family home in Cheshire had been raided by a gang of three burglars during the game, and only found out as United set off for Manchester. Thankfully, his wife Ana and their two children were away on holiday.

It’s understood Carrick had already made the bold decision to drop Fernandes for the first time in five years, and make Harry Maguire captain against Bournemouth, even before hearing about his comments.

Despite liking an Instagram post saying ‘never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care’ after the Bournemouth defeat, Fernandes is said to have taken Carrick’s decision on the chin when the team was named on Saturday, just as he has accepted playing in a wider position over recent weeks while Youri Tielemans has stepped into the No 10 role.

Although Carrick and Fernandes were both at Carrington on Monday as speculation raged over the head coach’s future, the player had left before Carrick turned up just before 2pm. The Portuguese was having treatment on a niggling injury that has troubled him since the World Cup.

Once United had clarified Carrick’s position, the two men met at the training ground and cleared the air on Tuesday.

Carrick has since confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain and is set to lead the side against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge this lunchtime in what is a huge game for United and their manager.

Others have been less forgiving. Jamie Carragher branded Fernandes’ comments in Como ‘disgraceful’, while Alan Shearer believes he has tarnished his legacy at Old Trafford.

Carrick and Fernandes have cleared the air at Carrington and Fernandes will remain as United's captain, starting at Chelsea today

But the Portuguese's actions have reignited the debate over whether Fernandes is too emotional to wear the armband

The controversy has reignited the debate over whether Fernandes is too emotional to wear the armband. Former United boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer said so in a video clip that resurfaced last week, explaining why he preferred Maguire.

That was put to Carrick, who was part of Solskjaer’s coaching team at the time, and he said: ‘There are different personalities, characteristics and ways to lead.

‘The questions get asked, and I understand why you're asking them now. He cares deeply about this football club and about the team and he's desperate to do well.’

It is a view backed up by some sources who describe a football obsessive who takes United’s problems to heart and feels the pain of the alarming slump this season just as keenly as the fans. While other players have distractions away from the pitch (too many in Gary Neville’s opinion), they say Fernandes can find no escape.

He is understood to have been worn down by yet another United crisis just when it seemed the good times were coming back under Carrick. Inevitably, that has taken its toll and has not been helped by worries over his future at Old Trafford as talks over a new contract drag on.

Insiders describe him as ‘an emotional metronome’ who sets the mood around the club, both good and bad. They say he bonds the dressing room together, and question who else in the United squad should wear the armband.

However, some of Fernandes’ team-mates in recent years have seen him as a more divisive figure whose close relationship with Ruben Amorim was viewed with suspicion.

‘The players can be quite dismissive of him,’ said a source close to one. ‘Sometimes they roll their eyes when he’s talking.’

Not surprisingly, Fernandes’ form has suffered this season with his four goals and one assist coming in United’s only two wins against Ipswich Town and Sabah – months after he picked up the Premier League Player of the Year award for his nine goals and Premier League record 21 assists last term.

He brought his trophy into Carrington and posed for individual pictures with staff from the treatment room to the canteen to thank them for the part they played in his success.

‘The players can be quite dismissive of him,’ said a source close to one of Fernandes' team-mates. ‘Sometimes they roll their eyes when he’s talking’

Insiders describe him as ‘an emotional metronome’ who sets the mood around the club, both good and bad

‘He has been the club's best player over the past few seasons and we need to get the best out of him for this team to succeed,’ legendary United captain Bryan Robson told Daily Mail Sport.

‘I have always thought a captain should be a centre back or deep-lying midfielder so they can see the game and spot things when they go wrong.

‘The trouble for Bruno is he is playing in a more advanced position because we have no centre forward. He's constantly looking over his shoulder and not necessarily expending his energy in the right way.

‘He gets how important it is to keep the group together. I know he has been instrumental as captain in organising bonding dinners and days out. That helps, but he also must know the importance of keeping things in the dressing room.’

With the Como controversy behind him, Fernandes is said to have returned to being the best version of himself during what has been a turbulent week for everyone at United.

Stung by the reaction from fans on Sunday, he has taken what is described as ‘direct action’ to lift the rest of the players and confront the crisis, as a captain should. Now another test of his leadership awaits at Stamford Bridge.

#1296. Premier League: Man City Facing New Charges After Guilty Verdict

Manchester City are currently going through the appeal process after being found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations. But things could still get worse for the Citizens.

The Premier League announced in September that City had been found guilty of artificially inflating sponsorship deals during the nine years from 2009 to 2018.

City have maintained their innocence and the outcome of the appeal process is expected in the coming months. However, The Independent is now reporting that multiple executives want further investigations.

The Premier League are said to be facing a 'dilemma' as English football chiefs are pushing for further investigations into Man City's conduct.

More specifically, they are asking questions about the years that followed 2018. It is believed that directors are questioning whether the inflated sponsorship deals simply stopped in 2018, despite commercial income appearing to remain at the same level.

Manchester City could be in hot water with UEFA if they fail in their appeal against the Premier League's 115 financial charges.

In the original investigation, the Premier League found that Man City and the Abu Dhabi-based sponsors were 'related parties'. If it was proven that was still the case after 2018, then there would be a basis for further sanctions related to the seasons that followed.

The ongoing legal case began in 2023, when the Premier League accused the Manchester-based club of breaking115 financial charges after documents were leaked.

Now, executives don't believe the period after 2018 haven't been addressed adequately. However, the English top flight has taken a stance of not addressing the court case until it has reached a conclusion.

Potential punishments have been widely discussed since the guilty verdict. They have included large fines, transfer bans, titles being stripped, relegation and points deductions.

According to Football Insider, a single-season points deduction is the 'likely' course of action if the charges stick after City's appeal. The number of points is reported to be 'around 40 to 50 points'.

How much money Manchester City may need to pay 38 clubs in lost Premier League prize money

Previously, talkSPORT host and former footballer Alan Brazil claimed he'd been told a single-season points deduction was the punishment City would be handed. However, he claimed 60 points would be taken from them.

He said: "I’m hearing a 60-point deduction, which will please people and still give City a chance of surviving.

"I don’t know whether it’s this season. I can’t see how that can be this season because of the timing, when they get it through it’ll be too late. "Is it next season? But they are talking about a 60-point deduction."

Parkinson has worked wonders with the Red Dragons over the years, and he is a big reason why Wrexham find themselves playing in the Championship today. He even led them to within a whisker of the playoffs last season, but there have been no signs of progress this season.

That's despite Wrexham spending another £33.5million this summer, taking their spending totals for the last two summers up to £66.5million, which is a gigantic spend for a Championship club.

Expectations have risen and Parkinson is struggling to keep up. There has long been a debate about the style of football Parkinson has employed, and the vintage nature of it, but as the current Wrexham boss has found out, such complaints disappear quickly when there is success.

It does, however, make managers like Parkinson more susceptible to criticism when things are not going well, and that is the case currently. Fans are starting to wonder whether Parkinson has taken Wrexham as far as he can, and while his past achievements will buy Parkinson more time than most, even he knows Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney will have a decision to make if things continue on the current path.

He said after Wrexham's latest defeat, against Sheffield United: "It's probably as big an achievement last year as getting promotion in the other years, coming seventh in the Championship. Of course, we all know that the second season in the division, there's all that about the momentum was with us and there's a possibility that's a factor.

"But we are in a similar position to last year. Now my job and the rest of the staff's job is to understand as a group that we have to turn up every week and if we don't win, the performance is at a level where the manager and the opposition say, 'you were difficult to play against tonight'. I don't think Chris (Wilder, the Sheffield United manager) is saying that in the first half."

If Wrexham sack Parkinson, the question becomes who next? There are a couple of names linked with the job, and Scott Parker is now off the table due to him heading to West Ham to replace Nuno Espirito Santo. Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones is linked but simply doesn't offer the step forward Wrexham require, while Rob Edwards hasn't proven himself as someone who could offer a step forward from Parkinson.

One potentially solid option is former Swansea City and Nottingham Forest boss Steve Cooper. Fans would have to forget the Swansea connection, but Cooper has a Championship promotion on his record, and he employs the sort of football that works in the second tier.

Why? Because he is flexible. Cooper's background coming up through the academies was heavily possession-based, but in senior football, he has typically adapted his system to win games. He has played all sorts of formations and without a requirement to dominate the ball. In short, he has his teams do what it takes to get results, which is vital in the Championship.

"Coaching is about doing things in a way that you believe in but it is also about living in the moment and adapting. In the modern game, teams play a couple of formations in one game, they can be effective playing in different ways. Football has never been so fluid."

Too many managers fail in the second tier because they have an ideal about football and how it should be played, but more often than not, it is not applicable during a long, hard Championship season where games pile up and pitches start to degrade up and down the league.

Cooper has that pragmatism to the way he manages, which is vital.

Combine that with the promotion and Premier League experience on his CV, and Wrexham have a strong candidate should they decide to call it a day with Parkinson.

Wrexham currently sit 21st in the Championship after five games, picking up just one victory.

#1294. These three red flags could unmask dodgy journals

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

Bibliometric databases review the journals they list to ensure they are indexing quality titles that do not engage in shady publishing practices.Credit: Hisayoshi Osawa/Getty

Researchers have identified three warning signs that suggest journals might be engaging in suspicious publishing activities. Using these, they have found dozens of titles indexed in the leading scholarly database Scopus that could be problematic.

The three red flags are, for any given journal in a single year: a doubling of publication output; having more than 70% of published articles originating from a single country; and having at least 15% of articles flagged by the Problematic Paper Screener, a free online tool.

Using titles extracted from the freely available database OpenAlex, the researchers identified 3,753 journals that met at least one of these criteria. They cross-referenced these with journals indexed in Scopus and found that, of those, 5% had been delisted. The findings were published in a preprint1 on 20 October.

Exposing predatory journals: anonymous sleuthing account goes public

Exposing predatory journals: anonymous sleuthing account goes public

The researchers, and research-integrity specialists, say that the signals help to identify journals that merit further investigation — but do not prove that titles are problematic. They serve as “rudimentary flags”, says Achal Agrawal, a co-author of the preprint and a freelance data scientist in Raipur, India. And they indicate the problems that databases face as poor publishing practices proliferate, he adds.

Bibliometric databases such as Scopus are important in the global research ecosystem because they inform many rankings used to evaluate individual researchers and institutions. Inclusion in Scopus, run by the Dutch publisher Elsevier, typically indicates that a journal is reputable.

Scopus regularly reviews the journals it lists, using a tool to spot signs of suspicious activities that suggest titles are churning out low-quality research that doesn’t adhere to accepted scholarly standards. These include “changes in publication volume and journal scope, unusual patterns in authorship and author collaboration, anomalous citation behaviour, and indications that a journal has become vulnerable to questionable content”, a spokesperson for Elsevier told Nature.

For flagged journals, Scopus then conducts “a careful, individual assessment of all available information, including consideration of the journal’s own response”, the spokesperson added. It removes journals that do not meet certain metrics thresholds. Scopus delisted 156 journals last year, and has removed 100 so far this year.

“No single signal, and no fixed threshold, determines the outcome,” Elsevier’s spokesperson said. “A signal is a prompt to investigate, and where needed the journal is put forward for re-evaluation” by Scopus’s content-selection board.

Hijacked journals are still a threat — here’s what publishers can do about them

Hijacked journals are still a threat — here’s what publishers can do about them

The study reported that the roughly 3,500 journals that have not been delisted together contributed more than half a million papers in the years that they were flagged by at least one signal. Nearly 300 journals were flagged by two signals and 28 journals by all three.

Each signal warrants a further look into the journal, but on its own is not “a definite decision to delist”, says Anna Abalkina, a research-integrity sleuth and social scientist at the Free University of Berlin. “There could be a lot of reasons why a journal duplicates the volume of publication.” For example, that often happens for a new journal, or as part of a publisher’s business plan, she says. But Abalkina thinks that a journal with all three red flags suggests suspicious activity that is difficult to find legitimate justification for.

Álvaro Cabezas Clavijo, who studies research evaluation at the International University of La Rioja in Logroño, Spain, agrees that the three signs should be interpreted with care. For instance, for small journals, having a large proportion of papers from one country might not be “a mark of questionable practices”.

#1293. Carrick: ‘Roma are a really good team, big game for Manchester United’

Michael Carrick admits Roma ‘are a really good team’ and will put Manchester United under pressure in the Champions League tonight, as he explains some unusual choices.

It kicks off at Old Trafford at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CEST).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Feyenoord vs. Inter on the Liveblog.

Lenny Yoro is available again after his suspension against Como, but Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu, Marcus Rashford, Manuel Ugarte and Luke Shaw are still out of action.

“It’s a big game, and it’s what you expect in this competition. [Roma] have had a really good start to the season and credit to them for that, they’re a really good team. It’s why we want to be in this competition, we want to challenge ourselves against good teams, and try to come out on top. It’s a big night for us,” Carrick told Amazon Prime UK via BBC Sport.

Lisandro Martinez was sent off at the weekend in the defeat to Chelsea and is dropped to the bench today.

“We have to pick a team. We have a good squad, we have decisions to make. We have changed one or two in recent weeks, so we made the decision to go with this team tonight.”

Kobbie Mainoo made his comeback from injury as a substitute over the weekend, and starts today with Carlos Baleba for a new partnership.

“We have some really good midfielders, and different combinations provide different strengths. Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba have played recently together. Kobbie is back fit, and we just felt it was a good stage to put him back in.

“You’d like to think that they complement each other with the attributes they both have, and I’m looking forward to seeing them tonight,” explained Carrick.

Manchester United have been on disastrous form, without a victory since the 4-0 Champions League result with Sabah FK on September 10.

That was followed by three draws and six defeats in all competition, including a crushing 4-1 loss on Italian soil against Como.

On the other hand, Roma lost only one game all season, 4-3 to Real Madrid when leading 3-1 going into the 82nd minute.

“They play man to man and press all over the pitch you never really get time on the ball. Their play never really settles. Roma are really good at what they do.”

Carrick was not only in the Manchester United side that beat Roma 7-1 in 2007, he also scored two goals alongside Cristiano Ronaldo.

“That’s a long time ago. I think tonight is a whole new Manchester United. It’s the next opportunity for us to win a football match, we are looking to do that, we need to do that, and tonight would be a good one to win,” he concluded.

#1291. Mbuemo Disaster: Man Utd Players Rated and Slated vs Roma

Manchester United produced a scintillating second half comeback to come from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in a Champions League classic on Tuesday.

The Italian side started on the front foot and smelt nerves around Old Trafford, pressing from the front and causing United to make errors.

And that is what happened as Roma pounced on a mistake from Kobbie Mainoo with Matias Soule producing the finishing touch to give the visitors an 11th-minute lead.

Soon after, United made another error at the back which led to Roma being given a huge opportunity to double their lead from the penalty spot. Donyell Malen took it with aplomb, slotting the ball into the bottom corner to put Gianpiero Gasperini's side 2-0 ahead and stun Old Trafford.

The immediate response from the Reds was not what Carrick would have wanted, though he did get one after half-time with United coming out with a point to prove.

Bruno Fernandes halved the deficit from the penalty spot at the second attempt, and that gave United some momentum to get back into the game.

After Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire missed guilt-edge chances to equalise for United, Matheus Cunha stepped up to the plate and levelled, slotting home after a mistake from Roma.

Then Cunha became the new hero at United as he scored his second and the Reds' third to put them 3-2 in front, completing the comeback with a powerful strike which flew in off the post.

Although Cunha's evening ended on a sour note with a red card for two quick-fire bookable offences, United held on for a much-needed win for Carrick.

Manchester United were taking on AS Roma in the Champions League.

Has faced criticism following the mistake against Bournemouth and mixed performance at Chelsea on Saturday, but Lammens wasn’t at fault for either of Roma’s two goals.

The first was an inch-perfect finish from Soule, giving him no chance. Meanwhile, Malen’s spot-kick was right in the corner and Lammens had dived the other way.

He prevented Roma from scoring a third before half-time with a smart save to stop Malen’s low driven shot, before getting up to stop Rodrigo Mora’s rasping drive.

Like Lammens, Yoro has had his fair share of criticism from fans and pundits alike, but he was United’s best defender against Roma.

Yes, that didn’t take much, but he did his job when required. He made a good early tackle to deny the visitors and stopped them scoring a third, as he sprinted back to get in position before sliding to make a clearance, just as Mora was about to shoot.

Improved as the game wore on, but made a huge mistake leading to Roma’s penalty. His clearance was scuffed and went straight to Soule before his effort struck Ayden Heaven’s hand and referee Jesus Gil Manzano pointed straight to the spot.

As he usually is, Maguire was a nuisance from set pieces in the second half and caused Roma so many issues. But the visitors defended corners and crosses well.

With Lisandro Martinez dropped after his red card against Chelsea on Saturday, Heaven was handed another massive chance to impress for Carrick.

But it’s fair to suggest he didn’t take it. There were some positive moments, but he struggled for the most part, giving the penalty away and making other errors.

Worked hard and was industrious, but got caught up high leading to Roma’s first goal. As United lost possession, Dalot was in an advanced position and allowed Soule so much room to collect the ball and pick out a spot without being challenged.

Like Maguire, he grew into the game and defended well at times. Indeed, Dalot won NINE duels throughout, more than any other United player.

Gave United good energy in midfield and was neat in possession, but his night was ended in the 51st minute after he pulled up with a hamstring injury.

The ex-Brighton man looked steady and composed in there alongside Kobbie Mainoo, and it would be a huge blow for United if he is out for the long-term.

Committed with his defensive and off-the-ball work, making tackles, winning fouls and then driving with the ball, but his passing flattered to deceive.

He gave the ball away leading to Roma’s first goal and had a passing accuracy of just 83 per cent, a statistic that must improve if he wants to take his game to the next level.

A difficult evening at the office for Amad, who was taken off in the 75th minute after having just one shot, making no key passes and two successful dribbles.

Shea Lacey grabbed an assist when he replaced Amad, and it appears he could take Amad’s place in the starting XI against Aston Villa on Saturday.

Scored United’s penalty at the second attempt and was back to his best in the second half. He was involved in absolutely everything good the Reds did, with Fernandes having four shots, making a team-high four key passes and playing seven passes into the final third.

Behind Cunha, he was United’s second best player on the pitch in that second half.

Wow. What a second half performance that was from Cunha. He was sensational and capped it off with a match-winning brace.

His first goal was a smart finish, capitalising on a huge mistake before keeping his composure and side-footing the ball into the back of the net. Then his second was another excellent strike, smashing the ball beyond the goalkeeper from a tight angle.

A disappointing performance from Mbeumo, who failed to impress up front and missed one big chance in the second half. He hit both posts after being played through on goal by Cunha, and has to be more clinical if he wants to be United's main man while Benjamin Sesko is out.

That was a much-needed win for Michael Carrick, and it will ease the immediate pressure on the United boss for the time-being, though they must back it up against Villa on Sunday.

Mbeumo, Heaven, and Amad were some of the standout disappointing performances, with Carrick saved by Brazilian Cunha.

#1289. Aston Villa threatening Jamie Carragher with legal action over 'insults' looks wild... but this is why club's billionaire owner Nassef Sawiris has had enough, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 07:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 08:54 EDT, 31 October 2026

Before billionaires Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens took control of Aston Villa in summer 2018, the club were staring into the abyss.

Villa had just lost the Championship play-off final to Fulham and facing another year without Premier League funds, the club’s financial future was uncertain.

Eight years later, Villa have qualified for the Champions League for the second year in three. In Unai Emery, they have one of the world’s best coaches.

Despite significant issues navigating Premier League and UEFA financial rules, they lifted the Europa League last season and look well-equipped to challenge for a top-five finish again this term. In Sawiris’ time, they have made two £100million sales – Jack Grealish to Manchester City for £100m in 2021, and Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for £117m last summer, while investing hugely in players and making Emery one of the world’s best-paid coaches. Villa are also taking the capacity of Villa Park past 50,000.

By any measure, this is a club on the rise and Sawiris should feel very proud of what they have achieved during his tenure.

So you can imagine his irritation when Emery, the club’s most valuable asset, is being pushed towards the Manchester United job by a high-profile pundit like Jamie Carragher, apparently because Villa is not big enough for him. That said, the post that landed on Villa’s X account at 10.16pm on Friday still took the breath away.

Aston Villa is a club on the rise and Sawiris (above) should feel very proud of what they have achieved during his tenure

Jamie Carragher has been pushing Unai Emery towards the Manchester United job on The Overlap podcast, claiming that Villa 'will never be' United (source: TheOverlap/YouTube)

‘Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

‘Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.’

It is unclear which ‘insults’ drove Sawiris to this step. Carragher has talked up Emery’s candidacy for United on different platforms and received the inevitable backlash from Villa supporters online. Carragher doubled down on his view on The Overlap podcast this week, in which he told ‘Aston Villa fans’ to ‘shut the f*** up.’

He continued: ‘But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

The former Liverpool and England defender eventually apologised for his comments on Saturday, writing on Twitter: 'I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans. My language this week was clumsy & wrong.

'I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!'

Villa have been mocked for this response but look at it from their point of view. The club feel that at every turn, the established order are trying to slow their progress. Consider the financial regulations that favour traditionally wealthy clubs who make money off the pitch, over those who succeed on it.

Imagine the frustration of finishing fourth in the Premier League, winning the Europa League and then having to sell six starters from the final.

Last season Villa finished fourth in the Premier League, won the Europa League and then had to sell six of their starters from the final

Threatening legal action against a pundit may look wild but it does not come from a clear blue sky. Like many of the billionaire class, Sawiris is a tough operator and has taken an increasingly hands-on role at Villa in recent years.

He drove the move to hire Emery in 2022 and he has been more and more involved in transfers. He has forged good, professional relations with some of football’s other key players, including super-agent Jorge Mendes and Chelsea chief Behdad Eghbali. Sawiris ensured Villa received a record fee for Rogers and he was also instrumental in the capture of 18-year-old winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. His ambition for Villa is limitless.

For seasons now, Villa have operated in what Sawiris may feel is an arbitrary financial straitjacket. Now he has to listen to ex-players with significant influence telling the world that Villa can never satisfy Emery’s ambition.

Carragher is probably guilty of nothing more than expressing an opinion, however crudely he may have done so. But if Sawiris is fed up of various voices and organisations trying to put Villa back in their box, then who can blame him?

#1288. Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.
